```solidity
    function updateDownsideProtected(uint128 downsideProtectedAmount) external {
        downsideProtected += downsideProtectedAmount;
    }
```
https://github.com/sherlock-audit/2024-11-autonomint/blob/main/Blockchain/Blockchian/contracts/Core_logic/CDS.sol#L829-L831
```solidity
    function _updateCurrentTotalCdsDepositedAmount() private {
        if (downsideProtected > 0) {
            totalCdsDepositedAmount -= downsideProtected;
            totalCdsDepositedAmountWithOptionFees -= downsideProtected;
            downsideProtected = 0;
        }
    }
```
https://github.com/sherlock-audit/2024-11-autonomint/blob/main/Blockchain/Blockchian/contracts/Core_logic/CDS.sol#L833-L839
`_updateCurrentTotalCdsDepositedAmount()` is used in functions like deposit() and withdraw() so a revert here will DOS users from depositing and withdrawing.

### Internal pre-conditions

_No response_

### External pre-conditions

_No response_

### Attack Path

1. Malicious user sets downsideProtected to a large value (greater than totalCdsDepositedAmount)
2. Users calling deposit() or withdraw() will be DOS'ed because a revert will happen in `_updateCurrentTotalCdsDepositedAmount()` due to underflow.

### Impact

Users are DOS'ed from interacting with the protocol so those who deposited have their assets frozen in the contract.

### PoC

_No response_

### Mitigation

Implement access control to updateDownsideProtected()
summary: This bug report discusses a vulnerability in the CDS.sol code that allows malicious users to manipulate the downsideProtected variable, which can cause a denial of service (DOS) attack on the system. This vulnerability was found by multiple users and can be exploited by setting downsideProtected to a large value. This can lead to a revert in functions like deposit() and withdraw(), causing users to be unable to interact with the protocol and potentially losing their deposited assets. The report recommends implementing access control to prevent this vulnerability.

title: H-7: Incorrect deducted cds deposit amount in withdrawUser
description:
Source: https://github.com/sherlock-audit/2024-11-autonomint-judging/issues/563 

## Found by 
0x37, valuevalk

### Summary

The calculation for `totalCdsDepositedAmount` in withdrawUser() is incorrect when the cds owners opt in liquidations. This will impact all calculations which are related with `omniChainData.totalCdsDepositedAmount`.

### Root Cause

When cds owners want to withdraw positions, we will try to deduct this position's cds deposit from the `omniChainData.totalCdsDepositedAmount`. If this cds deposit position is opt in the liquidation, one part of cds deposit has already been used in the liquidation process. So when cds owners want to withdraw, we should [deduct the left deposited amount](https://github.com/sherlock-audit/2024-11-autonomint/blob/main/Blockchain/Blockchian/contracts/lib/CDSLib.sol#L728-L729 from `omniChainData.totalCdsDepositedAmount`.

The problem is that when we update `totalCdsDepositedAmount`, we calculate via `params.cdsDepositDetails.depositedAmount - params.cdsDepositDetails.liquidationAmount`. We should notice that `params.cdsDepositDetails.liquidationAmount` is not the used liquidation amount from the cds owner. It stands for left liquidation amount for this position.

We should deduct the left deposit amount: `depositedAmount - (initialLiquidationAmount - liquidationAmount)`
```solidity
    function withdrawUser(
        CDSInterface.WithdrawUserParams memory params,
        CDSInterface.Interfaces memory interfaces,
        uint256 totalCdsDepositedAmount,
        uint256 totalCdsDepositedAmountWithOptionFees,
        mapping(uint128 liquidationIndex => CDSInterface.LiquidationInfo)
            storage omniChainCDSLiqIndexToInfo
    ) public returns (CDSInterface.WithdrawResult memory) {
          CDSInterface.LiquidationInfo memory liquidationData = omniChainCDSLiqIndexToInfo[i];
          uint128 share = (liquidationAmount * 1e10) / uint128(liquidationData.availableLiquidationAmount);
          params.cdsDepositDetails.liquidationAmount -= getUserShare(liquidationData.liquidationAmount, share);
}
```
```solidity
      totalCdsDepositedAmount -= (params.cdsDepositDetails.depositedAmount - params.cdsDepositDetails.liquidationAmount);
      params.omniChainData.totalCdsDepositedAmount -= (params.cdsDepositDetails.depositedAmount - params.cdsDepositDetails.liquidationAmount);

```

### Internal pre-conditions

N/A

### External pre-conditions

N/A

### Attack Path

N/A

### Impact

`omniChainData.totalCdsDepositedAmount` will be updated incorrectly. This will cause incorrect cds cumulative value's calculation. 
Cds owners may get the incorrect return value.

### PoC

N/A

### Mitigation

```solidity
totalCdsDepositedAmount -= depositedAmount - (initialLiquidationAmount - liquidationAmount);
```
summary: This bug report is about an issue with the calculation of a variable called `totalCdsDepositedAmount` in a function called `withdrawUser()` in a software project. The problem occurs when users withdraw their positions and have opted in for liquidations. This leads to incorrect calculations and affects other related calculations as well. The root cause of the issue is that the code is deducting the wrong amount from the `totalCdsDepositedAmount` variable. This is because the code is using the wrong variable to calculate the deduction. This results in incorrect values being returned to users and can impact the overall calculation of the variable. The report suggests a solution to fix the issue and prevent it from happening in the future.

title: H-6: Lack of lastEthPrice sync between different chains
summary: The bug report is about a lack of synchronization of the lastEthPrice between different chains in the Autonomint system. This can cause incorrect calculation of the cumulative value of CDS deposits, resulting in incorrect withdrawal amounts for users. The root cause of the issue is that the lastEthPrice is only updated in the current chain and not synced with other chains. This can lead to repeated calculation of gains/losses when users deposit or withdraw in different chains. The impact of this bug is incorrect calculation of the cumulative value, which can result in incorrect withdrawal amounts for users. The suggested mitigation is to sync the lastEthPrice with other chains to ensure accurate calculation of gains/losses.

title: H-5: cds owners can withdraw more than expected via manipulating excessProfitCumulativeValue
description:
Source: https://github.com/sherlock-audit/2024-11-autonomint-judging/issues/469 

## Found by 
0x37, 0x73696d616f, 0xAristos, Galturok, John44, Kral01, Laksmana, PeterSR, RampageAudit, Ruhum, Waydou, ZanyBonzy, newspacexyz, pashap9990, super\_jack, t.aksoy, theweb3mechanic, tjonair, valuevalk, volodya

### Summary

`excessProfitCumulativeValue` in withdraw() can be manipulated. Malicious users can manipulate this `excessProfitCumulativeValue` to withdraw more than expected.

### Root Cause

In [CDS.sol:withdraw](https://github.com/sherlock-audit/2024-11-autonomint/blob/main/Blockchain/Blockchian/contracts/Core_logic/CDS.sol#L279), cds owners can withdraw their usda deposit.

In withdraw(), there is one parameter `excessProfitCumulativeValue`, we will use this parameter `excessProfitCumulativeValue` to calculate the cds owner's possible profit. Although this parameter `excessProfitCumulativeValue` is signed by the admin, the signature and `excessProfitCumulativeValue` can be replayed. When different cds owners withdraw, they will get the different `excessProfitCumulativeValue` and `signature` from the protocol's backend server. Malicious users can choose any valid `excessProfitCumulativeValue`, `nonce` and `signature` from on-chain data.

Malicious users can choose one smaller `excessProfitCumulativeValue` to trigger withdraw() function. Malicious users can get more profit than expected.

```solidity
    function withdraw(
        uint64 index, // deposit index.
        uint256 excessProfitCumulativeValue,
        uint256 nonce,
        bytes memory signature
    ) external payable nonReentrant whenNotPaused(IMultiSign.Functions(5)) {
        if (!_verify(FunctionName.CDS_WITHDRAW, excessProfitCumulativeValue, nonce, "0x", signature)) revert CDS_NotAnAdminTwo();
```
```solidity
    function cdsAmountToReturn(
        address _user,
        uint64 index,
        uint128 cumulativeValue,
        bool cumulativeValueSign,
        uint256 excessProfitCumulativeValue
    ) private view returns (uint256) {
    ...
                    uint256 profit = (depositedAmount * (valDiff - excessProfitCumulativeValue)) / 1e11;
    ...
}
```

### Internal pre-conditions

N/A

### External pre-conditions

N/A

### Attack Path

N/A

### Impact

Malicious users can withdraw more profit than expected via manipulating the `excessProfitCumulativeValue` and `signauture`.

### PoC

N/A

### Mitigation

Enhance the signature check. One signature can only be used for one cds owner's specific deposit index.
summary: This bug report discusses an issue found in the `cds owners` function of the `CDS.sol` contract. It was discovered that malicious users can manipulate the `excessProfitCumulativeValue` parameter to withdraw more profit than expected. This is possible because the signature and `excessProfitCumulativeValue` can be replayed, allowing users to choose any valid values from the on-chain data. This manipulation can result in malicious users getting more profit than they are entitled to. To fix this issue, the signature check needs to be enhanced so that one signature can only be used for one specific deposit index.

title: H-4: odosAssembledData can be manipulated
description:
Source: https://github.com/sherlock-audit/2024-11-autonomint-judging/issues/345 

## Found by 
0x37, 0x73696d616f, 0xNirix, Laksmana, tjonair, volodya

### Summary

The signature in withDraw can be reused and this will cause users can choose one improper odosAssembledData and convert less collateral than expected.

### Root Cause

In [borrowing.sol:withDraw](https://github.com/sherlock-audit/2024-11-autonomint/blob/main/Blockchain/Blockchian/contracts/Core_logic/borrowing.sol#L281), borrowers can withdraw their collateral. If the current Ether price is larger than deposited Ether price, borrowers will not withdraw all collaterals. There will be some remaining collateral. These remaining collaterals will be swapped to USDT via odos router.

In one normal scenario, the protocol backend server will generate odos assembled data got from odos api, and sign the signature. The borrower will use this signed signature and `odosAssembledData` to trigger this `withDraw` function.

But the problem is that malicious users can choose one improper `odosAssembledData` and signature. Although we can not manipulate the `odosAssembledData` to any value we want, the backend servers will generate all kinds of `odosAssembledData` for different borrower's withdrawal. The malicious borrower can choose any `odosAssembledData` from all of these `odosAssembledData`.

For example:
1. Alice deposits WrsETH via depositTokens.
2. The Ether price increases, Alice wants to withdraw her collateral. Her borrow position's remaining collateral is 0.05 ether. Normally, Alice's `odosAssembledData` will swap 0.05 ether wrsETH to USDT. But Alice searches the valid used `odosAssembledData`, and find one `odosAssembledData` which input token amt is 0.01 ether. Alice uses used `odosAssembledData` to trigger her withdraw.
3. We will swap 0.01 ether wrsETH to USDT. This will cause some wrsETH locked in the contract.

```solidity
    function _withdraw(
        address toAddress,
        uint64 index,
        bytes memory odosAssembledData,
        uint64 ethPrice, // current ether price
        uint128 exchangeRate,
        uint64 withdrawTime
    ) internal {
    ...
        uint256 amountToSwap = result.collateralRemainingInWithdraw -
            collateralRemainingInWithdraw;
        if (amountToSwap > 0) {
            amountToSwap = (amountToSwap * 1 ether) / exchangeRate;
            treasury.swapCollateralForUSDT(depositDetail.assetName, amountToSwap, odosAssembledData);
        }
    ...    
}
```

### Internal pre-conditions

N/A

### External pre-conditions

N/A

### Attack Path

1. Alice deposits WrsETH via depositTokens.
2. The Ether price increases, Alice wants to withdraw her collateral. Her borrow position's remaining collateral is 0.05 ether. Normally, Alice's `odosAssembledData` will swap 0.05 ether wrsETH to USDT. But Alice searches the valid used `odosAssembledData`, and find one `odosAssembledData` which input token amt is 0.01 ether. Alice uses used `odosAssembledData` to trigger her withdraw.
3. We will swap 0.01 ether wrsETH to USDT. This will cause some wrsETH locked in the contract.

### Impact

When we swap the remaining collateral to USDT, we may swap only one part of remaining collateral to USDT. This will break our intent. Some remaining collateral will be locked in the contract, and the output USDT is less than expected.

### PoC

N/A

### Mitigation

`odosAssembledData` and `signature` should only be valid for one borrower's specific borrowing index.
summary: This bug report discusses a potential issue found in the code for a project called autonomint-judging. The issue is related to the ability for users to manipulate the odosAssembledData, which can result in them converting less collateral than expected. This is caused by a problem in the code where borrowers can withdraw their collateral, but if the current Ether price is higher than the deposited Ether price, some collateral may remain. This remaining collateral is then swapped to USDT using the odos router. The problem arises when malicious users can choose an improper odosAssembledData and signature, which can result in them only being able to swap a portion of their remaining collateral to USDT. This can lead to some collateral being locked in the contract and the output of USDT being less than expected. The report provides an example of how this can occur and suggests that the odosAssembledData and signature should only be valid for one borrower's specific borrowing index in order to mitigate this issue.

title: H-3: `Borrowing::redeemYields` debits `ABOND` from `msg.sender` but redeems to `user` using `ABOND.State` data from `user`
summary: The bug report discusses an issue with the `redeemYields` function in the `Borrowing` contract. This function incorrectly debits `ABOND` from the `msg.sender` instead of the `user` and uses the `user`'s data to calculate the amount to be withdrawn from an external protocol. This allows an attacker to repeatedly purchase `ABOND` and redeem yields from the `user` without debiting from their account. The root cause is a mistake in the code where the `msg.sender` is used instead of the `user`. The impact of this bug is that the ETH deposited in the external protocol can be drained and the value of `ABOND` will decrease. The report suggests enforcing `msg.sender` to be equal to `user` as a mitigation.

title: H-2: Potential Underflow in `withdrawInterest`
description:
Source: https://github.com/sherlock-audit/2024-11-autonomint-judging/issues/228 

## Found by 
0x73696d616f, 0xAadi, Audinarey, AuditorPraise, Aymen0909, Cybrid, Galturok, PeterSR, Ragnarok, RampageAudit, Waydou, nuthan2x, onthehunt, super\_jack, volodya

### Summary

In the `withdrawInterest` function, if `totalInterest` is less than `amount`, subtracting `amount` from `totalInterest` will cause an underflow and revert the transaction due to Solidity 0.8.x's checked arithmetic, even if `totalInterestFromLiquidation` has sufficient balance to cover the withdrawal.

### Root Cause

The function checks the combined balance but only subtracts from `totalInterest`:

https://github.com/sherlock-audit/2024-11-autonomint/blob/0d324e04d4c0ca306e1ae4d4c65f0cb9d681751b/Blockchain/Blockchian/contracts/Core_logic/Treasury.sol#L616C1-L625C6

```solidity
require(amount <= (totalInterest + totalInterestFromLiquidation), "Treasury don't have enough interest");
totalInterest -= amount;
```

If `totalInterest < amount`, this subtraction underflows and reverts.

### Internal pre-conditions

none

### External pre-conditions

none

### Attack Path

_No response_

### Impact

DOS, underflow and revert.

### PoC

1. Set `totalInterest` to 50 and `totalInterestFromLiquidation` to 100.
2. Attempt to withdraw an `amount` of 75.
3. The `require` passes because 75 ≤ 150.
4. Subtracting 75 from `totalInterest` (50) causes an underflow and reverts.

### Mitigation

Implement logic to deduct the `amount` from `totalInterest` and `totalInterestFromLiquidation` proportionally or sequentially:

```solidity
if (amount <= totalInterest) {
    totalInterest -= amount;
} else {
    uint256 remaining = amount - totalInterest;
    totalInterest = 0;
    totalInterestFromLiquidation -= remaining;
}
```
summary: This report discusses a bug found by multiple individuals in the `withdrawInterest` function of the Autonomint contract. The bug occurs when the amount being withdrawn is greater than the total interest available, causing an underflow and reverting the transaction. This is due to a miscalculation in the function's logic, where it checks the combined balance but only subtracts from one of the balances. This bug can lead to a denial of service attack and should be fixed by implementing a proportional or sequential deduction method.

title: H-1: After closing synthetix position we don't update global data for liquidations
summary: This report discusses a bug in the Autonomint protocol that occurs after an admin closes a synthetix position. The bug prevents global variables from being updated, which means that dCDS depositors and the protocol cannot benefit from the liquidation and potential gains. The root cause of the bug is that the function responsible for closing the position does not update the necessary global variables. This is in contrast to how the protocol handles liquidation type 1, where many values are updated to make the protocol aware of the liquidated position and its collateral. The bug occurs after a liquidation type 2 event, where a short position is submitted for the liquidated collateral and then closed by the admin without updating global variables. This has a significant impact on dCDS depositors, as they are unable to withdraw their portion of the liquidation. The report suggests updating the global variables after closing the position to mitigate this issue.

title: Fixed commitment scheme has incorrect time bounds check, so remains ineffective
summary: This bug report discusses an issue with the commitment scheme in a software. The problem is that the fix submitted for the issue "Commitment scheme does not prevent frontrunning" does not actually solve the problem. The proof of concept provided in the report shows that the timing check in the code is incorrect, allowing for frontrunning to occur. This means that someone can intentionally manipulate the system to gain an advantage over others. The report suggests a solution by changing the check for recent commits and also recommends adding the proof-of-concept to the test suite. The bug has been fixed in two different versions of the software.

title: Commitment scheme does not prevent frontrunning
summary: The KinoAccount9CharCommitMinter contract has a commitment scheme in place to prevent frontrunning, but it is not effective. This allows someone to insert their own commit and frontrun a transaction, resulting in them taking the name that was meant to be minted by someone else. This was demonstrated in a test where a frontrunner, Frank, successfully took the name that was supposed to be minted by Alice. The recommendation is to add a check in the mint function to prevent frontrunning on the current block. This issue has been fixed in a pull request, but a new bug was discovered during the review process. This new bug has also been fixed, so the issue is considered resolved.

title: Token bound account may not be deployed at the counterfactual address
summary:
The bug report is about an issue in the Kimap.sol code, specifically in the Kimap._mint() function. The function is supposed to deploy a token-bound account (TBA) at a specific address, but if another mint transaction is executed before it, the TBA is deployed at a different address. This goes against the ERC-6551 standard which requires TBAs to be deployed using the create2 opcode to ensure a deterministic address. 

The report includes a proof of concept that shows two TBAs being deployed at different addresses even though they have the same parameters, except for the KinoAccountProxy address. The recommendation is to deploy the KinoAccountProxy using CREATE2 to ensure that the TBA is deployed at a counterfactual address. 

The bug has been fixed in PR 19 by using a better way to deploy using CREATE2. However, there is another issue with the fix where if someone executes the exact CREATE2 call before the kinode, it will revert. The report suggests a different approach to deploying using CREATE2 to avoid this issue.

title: Genes are overrideable
summary: The bug report discusses an issue with the function "gene()" in the KinoAccountMinter contract. It is possible for the gene implementation to be changed at any time, even by child accounts. This means there is no difference between leaving the gene unset and setting a new gene before each use. A proof of concept is provided, along with a test that shows the issue with gene inheritance. The recommendation is to make genes immutable and this issue has been fixed in the latest update.

title: Calls to AccessHub.setFeeSplit will revert due to _feeSplits having the wrong type
description:
## AccessHub.setFeeSplit Function Overview

## Context
AccessHub.sol#L149

## Description
The `AccessHub.setFeeSplit` function allows `SWAP_FEE_SETTER` to set the fee splits for pools (either Continuous Liquidity or not). The `_feeSplits` parameter is an array that represents percentages. 

In the case of non-Continuous Liquidity (CL) pairs (managed by `poolFactory`), 100% is represented as 10,000. However, since `_feeSplits` is of type `uint8[]`, it can only facilitate a maximum percentage of 255/10,000 = 2.55% per pool. This limitation can result in some fees going unclaimed.

To summarize, calls to the function may lead to reversion or can leave unclaimed tokens.

## Recommendation
Consider changing the type of `_feeSplits` to `uint256[]`.

## Shadow Exchange
Fixed in commit fbdb3796.

## Cantina Managed
Verified.
summary: The AccessHub.sol#L149 function, AccessHub.setFeeSplit, has a bug where it can only facilitate a maximum percentage of 2.55% per pool, even though it is supposed to represent 100%. This means that some fees will not be claimed properly. The recommended solution is to change the type of _feeSplits to uint256[]. This bug has been fixed in commit fbdb3796 and verified by Cantina Managed. It is considered a medium risk bug.

title: Unchecked voting status in `moveVotes()` allows vote power inflation
description:
##### Description

- https://gitlab.ubertech.dev/blockchainlaboratory/eywa-dao/blob/39fba4bee623a3e60a529416f93d76e73658440d/contracts/EscrowManager.sol#L396

The `moveVotes()` method in `EscrowManager` does not validate whether the token has already voted by checking the `s_hasVotedByTokenId` mapping.

Because there is no check of `s_hasVotedByTokenId[tokenId_]` within `moveVotes()`, an attacker (or any user) can:
1. Cast a vote.
2. Call `moveVotes()` to move their votes (via `DELEGATION_MANAGER`).
3. Repeat the above sequence.

By doing so, the user could artificially inflate their voting power, effectively manipulating voting outcomes.

##### Recommendation

Add a validation check for `s_hasVotedByTokenId[tokenId_]` in the `moveVotes()` method, similar to the one in `_update()`. For instance (https://gitlab.ubertech.dev/blockchainlaboratory/eywa-dao/blob/39fba4bee623a3e60a529416f93d76e73658440d/contracts/EscrowManager.sol#L517):
```solidity
if (s_hasVotedByTokenId[tokenId_]) {
    revert LockCurrentlyVoting();
}
```

***
summary: The `moveVotes()` method in the `EscrowManager` contract does not properly check if a token has already voted before allowing it to move its votes. This means that an attacker or any user could cast a vote, move their votes, and repeat the process to artificially inflate their voting power and manipulate the outcome of a vote. To fix this, a validation check should be added to `moveVotes()` similar to the one in `_update()`. This will prevent tokens from voting multiple times and ensure fair voting outcomes.

title: Incorrect math in `EscrowManager.getPastVotes()`
description:
##### Description

Voting weight decreases over time at a fixed rate calculated based on the current deposit. However, the same rate is used to calculate past voting weight: the current voting weight is increased by the current rate multiplied by the elapsed time. The issue is that the current rate may not reflect the rate the user had in the past, leading to discrepancies in the calculated voting weight—either higher or lower—compared to the actual historical value.

We consider this a high issue because ProposalManager retrieves the user's voting power from the past. Depending on the proposal creation time, it may look for the user voting power rate from a previous epoch which can be calculated incorrectly.

https://gitlab.ubertech.dev/blockchainlaboratory/eywa-dao/-/blob/29465033f28c8d3f09cbc6722e08e44f443bd3b2/contracts/EscrowManager.sol#L421

In the provided PoC, the user deposits more funds, causing their past votes to decrease, even though they should remain unchanged:
```
await checkIncorrectPastVotes(
    "aliceTokenId3", "Common2", "eywa NFT locked without boost");
async function checkIncorrectPastVotes(
    aliceTokenId, 
    eywaTokenId, 
    description) {
describe(`Test`, () => {
    describe("Test", () => {
    it("Test", async () => {
        const { eywaNFT, escrowManager, alice, AliceTokenId, TokenId } = 
            await loadFixture(deploy);

        const blockNumber = await ethers.provider.getBlockNumber();
        const block = await ethers.provider.getBlock(blockNumber);

        console.log("Alice votes", 
            await escrowManager.getPastVotes(alice, block.timestamp))

        await network.provider.send("evm_increaseTime", [60 * 60 * 24 * 7 + 1])
        await network.provider.send("evm_mine")

        console.log("Alice votes", 
            await escrowManager.getPastVotes(alice, block.timestamp))
        await escrowManager.connect(alice).deposit(
            AliceTokenId[aliceTokenId], 10n ** 18n)
        console.log("Alice votes", 
            await escrowManager.getPastVotes(alice, block.timestamp))
        console.log("Alice votes", 
            await escrowManager.getPastVotes(alice, block.timestamp))
    })
    })
})
}
```

Output:
```
Alice votes 35185450688622750n
Alice votes 35185450688622750n
Alice votes 30782345402868525n
Alice votes 30782345402868525n
```

##### Recommendation

We recommend accurately accounting for past rate changes in the mathematical calculations.

***
summary: The bug report describes an issue where the voting weight for users is calculated incorrectly due to a fixed rate being used for both current and past voting weight. This can lead to discrepancies in the calculated voting weight compared to the actual historical value. The bug is considered high priority as it affects the ProposalManager and can result in incorrect calculations. A PoC (Proof of Concept) is provided to demonstrate the issue, where the user's past votes decrease even though they should remain unchanged. The recommendation is to accurately account for past rate changes in the mathematical calculations.

title: Incorrect transfer of ERC-20 tokens to non-compatible contract
description:
##### Description

- https://gitlab.ubertech.dev/blockchainlaboratory/eywa-dao/-/blob/29465033f28c8d3f09cbc6722e08e44f443bd3b2/contracts/EscrowVoteManagerV1.sol#L136

It was discovered that the `s_emissionManager` contract does not handle ERC20 tokens. However, the following code attempts to transfer ERC20 tokens to this contract:

```solidity
IERC20(s_eywa).safeTransfer(s_emissionManager, m_claimableRewards);
```

Since `s_emissionManager` is not designed to accept or manage ERC20 tokens, any tokens sent to it may become irretrievable.

##### Recommendation
We recommend modifying the contract logic to prevent ERC20 tokens from being transferred to `s_emissionManager` unless it is updated to handle ERC20 tokens properly.

***
summary: The bug report states that there is a problem with the `s_emissionManager` contract. This contract is not able to handle ERC20 tokens, which are a type of cryptocurrency. However, there is a code in the contract that tries to transfer ERC20 tokens to it. This means that any tokens sent to the contract may not be able to be retrieved. The recommendation is to change the contract so that it does not accept ERC20 tokens unless it is updated to handle them correctly.

title: `s_votesByPool[m_pool]` persists indefinitely, leading to rewards allocation after lock expiry
description:
##### Description
When a user votes in the `EscrowVoteManagerV1` contract, the value of **s_votesByPool[m_pool]** is incremented by the user's voting power.

https://gitlab.ubertech.dev/blockchainlaboratory/eywa-dao/blob/29465033f28c8d3f09cbc6722e08e44f443bd3b2/contracts/EscrowVoteManagerV1.sol#L307

However, this value does not decrease when the user's lock expires. Instead, it remains unchanged until the user explicitly interacts with one of the following functions.

1. `EscrowVoteManagerV1.vote()`
2. `EscrowVoteManagerV1.poke()`
3. `EscrowVoteManagerV1.reset()`

This behavior allows a user to create a lock, vote once, and ensure that the corresponding pool continues to benefit from their voting power indefinitely, even after the lock has expired. This occurs because the votes are not adjusted or re-evaluated unless the user takes further action.

Additionally, the gauge index is updated whenever new rewards are transferred to `EscrowVoteManagerV1`, which ensures that the gauge tied to the pool continues to receive rewards. This creates an inconsistency where expired locks still influence reward distribution.

https://gitlab.ubertech.dev/blockchainlaboratory/eywa-dao/-/blob/29465033f28c8d3f09cbc6722e08e44f443bd3b2/contracts/EscrowVoteManagerV1.sol#L356

It was also found that if calling `s_escrowManager.getVotesByTokenId(tokenId_)` (https://gitlab.ubertech.dev/blockchainlaboratory/eywa-dao/-/blob/29465033f28c8d3f09cbc6722e08e44f443bd3b2/contracts/EscrowVoteManagerV1.sol#L198) returns `0`, then no one can nullify the user's votes, due to the following revert (https://gitlab.ubertech.dev/blockchainlaboratory/eywa-dao/-/blob/29465033f28c8d3f09cbc6722e08e44f443bd3b2/contracts/EscrowVoteManagerV1.sol#L303):

```
if (m_votesForPool == 0) {
    revert ZeroEntry();
}
```

This way, the user will forever have votes for pools in `EscrowVoteManagerV1`.

##### Recommendation
We recommend implementing a mechanism that tracks users' votes on a per-epoch basis, similar to the approach used in the `IncentiveRewardsDistributor` and `RebaseRewardsDistributorV1` contracts.

***
summary: The bug report describes an issue with the `EscrowVoteManagerV1` contract where a user's voting power does not decrease when their lock expires. This allows them to continue influencing reward distribution indefinitely. Additionally, there is a problem where if a user's votes return as 0, they cannot be nullified, giving them permanent voting power. The report recommends implementing a mechanism to track votes on a per-epoch basis to fix these issues.

title: Protocol DoS via `EscrowVoteManagerV1.poke()`
summary: The bug report describes a problem where any user can use the `EscrowVoteManagerV1.poke()` function with a token that they do not own. This can cause issues with the protocol and disrupt its operations. The comments in the code suggest that this function is meant for changing voting power, but it can actually cause unexpected behavior and misuse. The report recommends restricting the function to only be used by the owner of the token.

title: Incorrect `ProposalManager.CLOCK()` behaviour
description:
##### Description
The `ProposalManager` contract interacts with `EscrowManager` as a **token**, but the `EscrowManager` contract does not implement the `CLOCK()` and `CLOCK_MODE()` methods.

When attempting to create a proposal using `ProposalManager.propose()`, the `clock()` method is invoked. The call to this method fails within the **try** block, causing the execution to enter the **catch** block. In the **catch** block, **block.number** is returned.

https://gitlab.ubertech.dev/blockchainlaboratory/eywa-dao/-/blob/29465033f28c8d3f09cbc6722e08e44f443bd3b2/contracts/ProposalManager.sol#L161

The snapshot is calculated as **block.number + votingDelay**. With the current **votingDelay** set to 2 days, this results in a very small snapshot value, which is not aligned with expected behavior. The **proposalSnapshot** then used in `Governor.castVote()` and `ProposalManager.state()` methods returns incorrect values due to this miscalculation.
##### Recommendation
We recommend modifying the catch block in the `CLOCK()` method to return **block.timestamp** instead of **block.number**.

***
summary: The `ProposalManager` contract is having issues when interacting with the `EscrowManager` contract. This is because the `EscrowManager` contract does not have the necessary `CLOCK()` and `CLOCK_MODE()` methods implemented. This causes problems when trying to create a proposal using the `ProposalManager.propose()` function, as it calls the `clock()` method which fails and returns the `block.number` instead of the expected `block.timestamp`. This leads to incorrect values being returned in the `proposalSnapshot` and other related methods. To fix this, it is recommended to modify the catch block in the `CLOCK()` method to return `block.timestamp` instead of `block.number`.

title: Incorrect logic in `GaugeV1.notifyRewardAmount()`
summary: The report highlights a bug in the `notifyRewardAmount()` function of the `GaugeV1` contract. The function uses an incorrect value for creating a Merkl campaign, which results in the loss of accumulated rewards for the gauge. The bug is caused by the function using the `balanceOf(address(this))` parameter instead of the `amount_` parameter, and also missing a `transferFrom()` call. The recommended solution is to implement functionality to transfer rewards from the `EscrowVoteManagerV1` contract to the `GaugeV1` contract.

title: Reentrancy in `EscrowManager`
summary: The OpenZeppelin ERC721 NFT implementation has a vulnerability that can be exploited by hackers. This vulnerability allows them to manipulate the boosting mechanism and gain an unfair advantage in voting power. This can happen when certain methods are called, such as `createLock()`, `deboost()`, and `withdraw()`, and the state of the `EscrowManager` is inconsistent. This can lead to corrupt storage variables and inaccurate calculations. The report provides a proof-of-concept example of how this can be done and recommends using certain approaches to prevent this type of reentrancy attack.

title: Duplicate voting via EscrowManager NFT transfers
summary: The `ProposalManager` contract has a bug where a user can transfer their voting power to another account and both accounts can vote on the same proposal using the same voting power. This can be exploited by an attacker to artificially increase the total votes for a proposal and potentially pass it without having the required voting power. It is recommended to fix this issue by ensuring that each voting NFT token can only be used once per proposal, even if transferred.

title: Incorrect checkpoint handling nullifies voting weights
description:
##### Description
- https://gitlab.ubertech.dev/blockchainlaboratory/eywa-dao/blob/29465033f28c8d3f09cbc6722e08e44f443bd3b2/contracts/EscrowManager.sol#L869

A vulnerability has been identified in the `_findCheckpoint` method of the `EscrowManager` contract, where it incorrectly handles checkpoints that occur within the same `block.timestamp`. When the current timestamp equals the timestamp of the checkpoint `[currentCheckpointNumber - 1]`, the same token is added to the tokenIds array, and `s_checkpointsNumberByAccount` is incremented by one. As a result, this creates a checkpoint with an empty `tokenIds` array.

When multiple checkpoints share the same timestamp, the method erroneously retrieves the current value instead of the correct historical value. This issue arises because `s_checkpoints[account_][m_checkpointsNumber - 1].timestamp == block.timestamp` leads to improper retrieval logic.

The `_moveVotes` function (see [EscrowManager.sol#L723](https://gitlab.ubertech.dev/blockchainlaboratory/eywa-dao/-/blob/29465033f28c8d3f09cbc6722e08e44f443bd3b2/contracts/EscrowManager.sol#L723)) does not account for this condition, causing an error where `m_oldTokenIds == s_checkpoint.tokenIds`. This inconsistency leads to `++s_checkpointsNumberByAccount[to_]` pointing to a non-existent array element, effectively corrupting the vote tracking mechanism.

An attacker can exploit this vulnerability to nullify any user's votes by performing actions that create multiple checkpoints at the same `block.timestamp`. For instance, by transferring a minimal amount (e.g., `1 wei` of EYWA tokens) to the target user's account multiple times within the same block, the attacker can reset the user's voting power to zero.

**Attack Example:**
```javascript
// Hardhat configuration: allowUnlimitedContractSize: true
await escrowManager.connect(alice)["createLock(uint256,uint256,address)"](
    1, lockDuration, bob.address);
await escrowManager.connect(alice)["createLock(uint256,uint256,address)"](
    1, lockDuration, bob.address);

console.log("getVotes(bob)", await escrowManager.getVotes(bob.address));
// Output: 0
```
In this example, Alice creates two locks for Bob within the same block timestamp, resulting in Bob's votes being reset to zero.

##### Recommendation
We recommend avoiding increments to the `s_checkpointsNumberByAccount` mapping when changes occur at the same timestamp. Additionally, ensure that the same token is not pushed into the tokenIds array if it already exists within the same checkpoint.


***
summary: The report describes a bug found in the `_findCheckpoint` method of the `EscrowManager` contract. This bug occurs when multiple checkpoints are created at the same time, causing the method to retrieve the wrong historical value. This can be exploited by an attacker to reset a user's voting power to zero. To fix this, it is recommended to avoid increments to the `s_checkpointsNumberByAccount` mapping and ensure that duplicate tokens are not added to the tokenIds array.

title: Missing validation of vesting wallets in `EscrowManager.createLock()`
summary: The bug report describes a vulnerability in the `EscrowManager.createLock()` function. This function does not properly check the addresses of the vesting wallets, which can be exploited by an attacker to artificially increase their voting power in the system. The report recommends implementing a validation process for the wallet addresses, such as whitelisting or using a factory. This will prevent the use of "poisoned" wallets and make the system more secure.

title: Flaw in Redemption Price Calculation
description:
##### Description
A critical issue was uncovered in the `redeem` function of the `UsrRedemptionExtension` contract. The flaw lies in the way the `redeemPrice` is determined. The current code fetches the `redeemPrice` as the cost of 1 USDC in USR, mistakenly multiplying this price by the USR amount, which leads to incorrect calculations and loss for the protocol or users. For instance, if the USDC market price rises to $1.03, for 100 burned USR, the user will receive 103 USDC, which at the new market price would be approximately $106. This flaw can lead to users receiving more than intended or less in cases of USDC price decrese. The issue is classified as of **critical** severity due to its potential for financial impact.

##### Recommendation
We recommend modifying the code to divide by `redeemPrice` instead of multiplying it, thereby ensuring the price calculation aligns with potential market fluctuations of USDC.
summary: Critical issue in the `redeem` function of the `UsrRedemptionExtension` contract. The `redeemPrice` is calculated incorrectly, leading to incorrect calculations and potential financial loss for the protocol or users. The issue is classified as critical and it is recommended to modify the code to divide by `redeemPrice` instead of multiplying it to align with market fluctuations.

title: [H-01] Vyper is Not Sent To The Treasury In `BuyAndBurn.swapDragonXToVyperAndBurn()` Function
summary: This bug report discusses a high-risk issue in the `BuyAndBurn.swapDragonXToVyperAndBurn()` function. The code currently only sends 8% of the swapped DragonX tokens to the `LIQUIDITY_BONDING_ADDR` and the rest is burned. However, the code that transfers 50% of the tokens to the `vyper.treasury()` is commented out. This means that too many funds are being burned and the treasury will not receive any funds. The recommendation is to uncomment the code to allow transfers to the Vyper treasury. The team has responded that the issue has been fixed.

title: Incorrect Fee Determination
description:
##### Description

The `_fillOrders` function uses the `exOrderId` parameter to determine if the trade pair is zero-fee by calling `orderBookConfig.isPairZeroFee`. This is incorrect because `isPairZeroFee` is meant to operate on `pairId`, which uniquely identifies the trade pair, not on `exOrderId`.

This issue can lead to:

1. **Incorrect Fee Application**: Trades may incorrectly bypass fees or be charged when they shouldn't be, depending on the misinterpretation of `exOrderId`.
2. **Financial Discrepancies**: The mismatch could result in imbalanced settlements and potential fund mismanagement.
3. **Exploitable Behavior**: Malicious actors might craft orders with specific `exOrderId` values to manipulate the fee logic.

##### BVSS

[AO:A/AC:L/AX:L/C:N/I:M/A:L/D:N/Y:N/R:N/S:C (7.0)](/bvss?q=AO:A/AC:L/AX:L/C:N/I:M/A:L/D:N/Y:N/R:N/S:C)

##### Recommendation

In `_fillOrders`, replace the reference to `exOrderId` in the `isPairZeroFee` call with `pairId`:

```
vars.isZeroFee = orderBookConfig.isPairZeroFee(takerOrder.pairId);

```

This ensures that the fee determination correctly evaluates based on the trading pair and not an unrelated order identifier. This change will preserve the integrity of the fee mechanism and prevent unintended financial impacts or exploit opportunities.

##### Remediation

**SOLVED**: The code is now using `pairId.`

##### Remediation Hash

5e97e95331149fbfb2986afabf65aba5ec0e23d2
summary: The `_fillOrders` function in the code uses the wrong parameter to determine if a trade pair is zero-fee, which can cause various issues. This includes incorrect fees being applied, financial discrepancies, and potential exploitation by malicious actors. To fix this, the code should be updated to use the correct parameter, `pairId`, to ensure the fee determination is accurate and prevent any unintended consequences. This issue has been resolved by updating the code and the fix can be identified by the hash 5e97e95331149fbfb2986afabf65aba5ec0e23d2.

title: Missing checks cause DoS & consistent failed redemptions in IntentTokenMinting
summary: The `IntentTokenMinting.sol` contract has a vulnerability that allows external calls to the `QuotaController.sol` contract without proper access control. This can be exploited by a malicious user to consume the daily quota of other users, potentially causing Denial of Service (DoS) for legitimate redemptions. The recommendation is to implement access control to restrict the `checkQuota` function to only be called by the `IntentTokenMinting.sol` contract. This issue has been resolved by the dappOS team in commit hash `3739b73fcbb41d7ccc3b3133b94a37286141e02d.`

title: Auto redemption functionality broken by incorrect address passed to `SmartVaultV4::autoRedemption`
description:
**Description:** `SmartVaultV4::autoRedemption` has the following signature:

```solidity
function autoRedemption(
    address _swapRouterAddress,
    address _quoterAddress,
    address _collateralToken,
    bytes memory _swapPath,
    uint256 _USDCTargetAmount,
    address _hypervisor
)
```

However the invocation in `AutoRedemption::fulfillRequest` incorrectly passes the vault address in place of the swap router address:

```solidity
IRedeemable(_smartVault).autoRedemption(
    _smartVault, quoter, _token, _collateralToUSDCPath, _USDsTargetAmount, _hypervisor
);
```

**Impact:** Auto redemption functionality will become completely broken when attempting to repay the debt of a non-legacy vault.

**Recommended Mitigation:** Pass the correct swap router address stored in the `SmartVaultManagerV6` contract.

**The Standard DAO:** Fixed by commit [4400e25](https://github.com/the-standard/smart-vault/commit/4400e25c87880b7ab1b5d19fbe520e4db5b70122).

**Cyfrin:** Verified. The correct `swapRouter` address is now passed.

\clearpage
summary: The `autoRedemption` function in the SmartVaultV4 contract has a bug where the vault address is incorrectly passed instead of the swap router address. This will cause problems when trying to repay the debt of a non-legacy vault. To fix this, the correct swap router address should be passed from the SmartVaultManagerV6 contract. The issue has been resolved in the Standard DAO by commit 4400e25 and verified by Cyfrin.

title: `AutoRedemption::fulfillRequest` should never be allowed to revert
description:
**Description:** Given that the Chainlink Functions DON will not retry failed fulfilments, `AutoRedemption::fulfillRequest` should never be allowed to revert; otherwise, `lastRequestId` will not be reset to `bytes32(0)` which means `AutoRedemption::performUpkeep` will never be able to trigger new requests.

Currently, inline comments suggest that there is an intention to revert if the Chainlink Functions DON returns an error; however, this should be avoided for the reason explained above. Similarly, any potential malformed response or reverts caused by external calls should be handled gracefully and fall through to this line:

```solidity
lastRequestId = bytes32(0);
```

**Impact:** Complete DoS of the auto redemption functionality.

**Recommended Mitigation:** * Do __not__ revert if an error is reported.
* Validate the response against its expected length to ensure that the decoding does not revert.
* Handle reverts from all external calls using `try/catch` blocks.
* Short-circuit if `AutoRedemption::calculateUSDsToTargetPrice` returns `0` (since this will cause the swap to [revert](https://github.com/Uniswap/v3-core/blob/main/contracts/UniswapV3Pool.sol#L603)).
* Optionally add an access-controlled admin function to reset `lastRequestId`.

**The Standard DAO:** Fixed by commit [5235524](https://github.com/the-standard/smart-vault/commit/523552498edefe77aa2782d2a887bb1980cf80b9).

**Cyfrin:** Verified. The response length is now validated against its expected length, which will also result in the logic being skipped if an error is reported. `AutoRedemption::runAutoRedemption` will only run if the target `USDs` amount is non-zero and other reverts from external calls are handled using `try/catch` blocks. An admin function to forcibly reset `lastRequestId` has not been added.
summary: This bug report is about a problem with the Chainlink Functions DON, which is causing the auto redemption feature to not work properly. This means that requests are not being reset, which is preventing new requests from being triggered. This bug can cause a complete denial of service for the auto redemption feature. The recommended solution is to not revert if there is an error, validate the response length, handle reverts from external calls, and add an admin function to reset the requests. The bug has been fixed by a commit and verified by another source.

title: Auto redemption logic can be abused by an attacker due to insufficient access control
description:
**Description:** `AutoRedemption::performUpkeep` is exposed for use by the Chainlink Automation DON when upkeep is required:

```solidity
function performUpkeep(bytes calldata performData) external {
    if (lastRequestId == bytes32(0)) {
        triggerRequest();
    }
}
```

However, there is an absence of access control that allows the function to be called by an address. Since `lastRequestId` is reset to `bytes32(0)` at the end of `AutoRedemption::fulfillRequest` execution, this means that upkeep can be repeatedly performed after the previous one has succeeded, regardless the trigger condition.

If `AutoRedemption::fulfillRequest` reverts, the `lastRequestId` state will not be reset which completely blocks all future auto redemptions due to the conditional in `AutoRedemption::performUpkeep` shown above. Combined with the use of `ERC20::balanceOf` within both `SmartVaultV4Legacy::autoRedemption` and `SmartVaultV4::autoRedemption` to determine the amount `USDs` repaid, an attacker can force this DoS condition by sending a small amount of `USDs` directly to the target vault:

```solidity
uint256 _usdsBalance = USDs.balanceOf(address(this));
minted -= _usdsBalance;
```

This causes the vault balance to be inflated above the expected maximum `minted` amount and execution to revert due to underflow. Since the Chainlink Functions DON will not retry failed fulfilment, there will be no way to reset the state and recover core functionality without complete redeployment.

**Impact:** An attacker can repeatedly trigger auto redemption regardless of the trigger condition and without relying on price oracle manipulation. This could amount to a loss of funds to the protocol since the Chainlink subscription will be billed on every fraudulent fulfilment attempt. Alternatively, an attacker could completely block functionality of the auto redemption mechanism if fulfilment is made to revert.

**Recommended Mitigation:** * Re-check the trigger condition within `AutoRedemption::performUpkeep` and also consider adding [access control](https://docs.chain.link/chainlink-automation/guides/forwarder).
* Calculate the amount of `USDs` repaid as the balance diff rather than using the vault balance directly.

**The Standard DAO:** Fixed by commit [5ec532e](https://github.com/the-standard/smart-vault/commit/5ec532e5f3813a865102501dbb91cf13a0813930).

**Cyfrin:** The trigger condition is re-checked and a TWAP has been implemented, however:
* It is recommended to use a substantially large interval (at least 900 seconds, if not 1800 seconds) to protect against manipulation. Note: Uniswap V3 pool oracles are not multi-block MEV resistant.
* The `USDs` repayment amount calculation has not been modified to use balance diffs instead of direct `balanceOf()`.

**The Standard DAO:** Fixed by commit [a8cdc77](https://github.com/the-standard/smart-vault/commit/a8cdc77d1fac9817128e1f3c1c8a1ab57f715513), using the amount out of the swap rather than balance checks.

**Cyfrin:** Verified. The TWAP interval has been increased and the redeemed amount has been modified to use the value output from the swap.
summary: The bug report discusses an issue with a function called `AutoRedemption::performUpkeep` that is used by a program called the Chainlink Automation DON. The problem is that there is no control over who can use this function, so it can be called by anyone. This can cause problems because the function can be repeatedly used, even after it has already been successful. This can lead to a loss of funds for the program and can also block its functionality. The report recommends fixing this issue by adding access control and using a different method to calculate the amount of funds being repaid. The problem has been fixed by the Standard DAO, but another program called Cyfrin still needs to make some changes.

title: `AutoRedemption` mappings are not and can never be populated
description:
**Description:** The following mappings are declared within the `AutoRedemption` contract:

```solidity
mapping(address => address) hypervisorCollaterals;
mapping(address => bytes) swapPaths;
```

However, they are never populated and there are no public functions capable of doing so either.

When a request is triggered, `lastRequestId` is assigned a non-zero identifier:

```solidity
 lastRequestId = _sendRequest(req.encodeCBOR(), subscriptionID, MAX_REQ_GAS, donID);
```

But the execution of `AutoRedemption::fulfillRequest` will revert due to empty swap paths, so the `lastRequestId` storage will not be reset:

```solidity
bytes memory _collateralToUSDCPath = swapPaths[_token];
...
lastRequestId = bytes32(0);
```

Given the condition within `AutoRedemption::performUpkeep` that there must not be an existing unfulfilled request when creating a new one, this completely blocks all functionality and necessitates a complete redeployment.

**Impact:** Core auto redemption functionality will be broken for all vaults and cannot be fixed without redeployment.

**Recommended Mitigation:** Either:
* Pre-populate the mappings,
* Add access-controlled setter functions, or
* Query state from the `SmartVaultYieldManager` contract.

**The Standard DAO:** Fixed by commit [d72cdce](https://github.com/the-standard/smart-vault/commit/d72cdceed7d60c30abf329e1b8338bb5b13bca2b).

**Cyfrin:** Verified. The setter functions have been added.
summary: The report discusses a bug in the `AutoRedemption` contract where two mappings, `hypervisorCollaterals` and `swapPaths`, are not being used. This causes a problem when a request is made, as the `lastRequestId` storage is not reset due to empty swap paths. This prevents the core auto redemption functionality from working and requires a redeployment to fix. To mitigate this issue, the report suggests pre-populating the mappings, adding access-controlled setter functions, or querying state from the `SmartVaultYieldManager` contract. The bug has been fixed by the Standard DAO and verified by Cyfrin, with the addition of setter functions.

title: Vaults can be made erroneously liquidatable due to incorrect swap path
summary: This bug report discusses an issue with the auto redemption feature in the Uniswap v3 view-only quoter. When this feature is executed, the swap path of `collateral -> USDC` is incorrect when attempting to swap to `USDs`. This results in the vault becoming liquidatable if a sufficient amount of the collateral token is swapped. The recommended solution is to ensure the swap path is correct and add a check to prevent significant decreases in vault collateralization. The bug has been fixed by The Standard DAO through code changes. Cyfrin has verified the fix and confirms that the swap paths are now configured correctly.

title: Hypervisor collateral redemption can cause vaults to become undercollateralized due to slippage
summary: The report describes a bug in the redemption process for Hypervisor collateral. When redeeming, the `SmartVaultV4::autoRedemption` function calls `SmartVaultYieldManager::quickWithdraw` which withdraws the collateral without applying the additional protocol withdrawal fee. After redemption, the excess collateral is redeposited to the Hypervisor through `SmartVaultV4::redeposit`, which also does not apply the fee. This can result in undercollateralized vaults if an attacker takes advantage of the lack of slippage handling. To fix this, additional validation should be added to prevent vaults from becoming undercollateralized. The bug has been fixed by The Standard DAO, but Cyfrin suggests handling the case where vault debt is fully repaid to avoid division by zero. The Standard DAO has addressed this issue as well.

title: SecuritizeVault's share token is in wrong decimals
summary: This bug report discusses an issue with the `SecuritizeVault` contract, which is based on the `ERC4626Upgradeable` contract from OpenZeppelin. The problem arises when the vault uses external redemption and the liquidation token is different from the asset token. This causes inconsistencies in decimal handling, resulting in incorrect share token amounts being received by users. The report includes a proof of concept test case and recommends two possible solutions to mitigate the issue. The bug has been fixed by the Securitize team and verified by Cyfrin.

title: Mismatch in multiplier position causes incorrect weight calculations in `QuantAMMWeightedPool`
summary: The report describes a bug in QuantAMM weighted pools where the weights and multipliers are not being read correctly during updates. This results in incorrect weights being applied during token swaps, which can lead to unintended and potentially harmful outcomes for users. The bug has been fixed in the latest commits.

title: Incorrect handling of negative multipliers in `QuantAMMWeightedPool` leads to underflow in weight calculation
summary: This bug report discusses an issue in the code for the QuantAMMWeightedPool contract in the QuantAMM-V1 repository. The code contains a function called `calculateBlockNormalisedWeight` which has a section that can cause a problem. If the multiplier used in this function is negative and the time since the last update is not zero, it can result in a failed swap due to underflow. This can be reproduced by adding a specific test to the code. To fix this issue, the code should be modified to multiply by -1 before calculating the result. This bug has been fixed in a recent commit and has been verified by the Cyfrin team.

title: Token Index error in `getNormalizedWeights` calculates incorrect weight leading to incorrect pool asset allocation
summary: The `_getNormalizedWeights()` function in `QuantAMMWeightedPool.sol` has an error that affects the weight calculations for pools with more than 4 tokens. This can lead to incorrect asset allocation and has been fixed in the latest update.

title: Misconfigured index boundaries prevent certain swaps in QuantAMMWeightedPool
summary: The report describes a bug in the QuantAMM protocol where swaps involving certain tokens cannot be performed correctly. The issue is caused by incorrect conditions in the code, which can lead to underflow and array out-of-bounds errors. To fix the bug, the code needs to be refactored and the conditions need to be updated. The bug has been fixed in the latest version of the protocol.

title: ExternalFee contract treats newly deposit vault share as yield and charge performance fee on user deposit amount immediately
summary: The bug report discusses an issue with a ERC4626 strategy for a token called A. Users can deposit the underlying asset or the ERC4626 share directly. However, when depositing the share, the ExternalFee contract charges a performance fee immediately, even though there may not be any assets in the strategy. This is because the contract treats the newly deposited share as yield. As a result, the user's deposit amount is immediately reduced. To fix this issue, the report recommends not counting new vault shares as yield during deposits, and making changes to the approach used for transfers. The risk level for this bug is medium.

title: Donated reward token can overﬂow the yieldAccumulator and revert user withdraw trans- action
summary: The bug report describes an issue with a proof of concept code in EarnVault.t.sol. The code is supposed to create a position and withdraw funds, but when tested, it fails with an error related to an overflow in the yield accumulator. This is due to a donation of tokens that increases the balance and causes the accumulator to exceed its maximum value. The report recommends a fix and notes that a previous fix for a similar issue may also solve this problem. Another reviewer confirms that the fix looks good, but mentions that the donated token can still cause problems.

title: The hint is not fetched properly from lido withdrawal queue and make all lido delayed with- draw revert
description:
## LidoSTETHDelayedWithdrawalAdapter.sol

## Context
LidoSTETHDelayedWithdrawalAdapter.sol#L173-L175

## Description
```solidity
uint256[] memory hints = _queue.findCheckpointHints(requestsToClaim, 1, requestsToClaim.length + 1);
```
The `hints` are fetched using the code above. According to the code and docs:

```solidity
function findCheckpointHints(uint256[] _requestIds, uint256 _firstIndex, uint256 _lastIndex)
view
returns (uint256[] hintIds)
```

### Requirements
- Array of request ids must be sorted.
- `firstIndex` must be greater than 0, because the checkpoint list is a 1-based array.
- `_lastIndex` must be less than or equal to `getLastCheckpointIndex()`.

Note how the `_lastIndex` is passed in. The last index is passed as `requestsToClaim.length + 1`, not `getLastCheckpointIndex()`.

### Cases

#### Case 1: `requestsToClaim.length < getLastCheckpointIndex()`
Assume the user wants to withdraw 5 requests, and `requestsToClaim.length + 1` will be 6, but the current `getLastCheckpointIndex()` returns 562 (see contract `0x889edc...12f9b1` on Ethereum mainnet).  
Then, the hints will always be 0.

#### Case 2: `requestsToClaim.length > getLastCheckpointIndex()`
This case is rare, but the transaction just reverts when querying the hint. We can work through an example (see transaction `0xcaee15...7f20ba` on Ethereum mainnet).

This is a withdrawal transaction:
- Request id: 59498
- hints: 555

If we query `findCheckpointsHints` in the contract `0x889edc...12f9b1`, we pass in:
- Request id: 59498
- First index: 1
- Last index: 2

We get 0; the last index is too short and we get no hints. 

The `getLastCheckpointIndex()` is 562. We pass in:
- Request id: 59498
- First index: 1
- Last index: 562

We get the hint value 555 correctly, which matches the withdrawal hint. But if we pass in:
- Request id: 59498
- First index: 1
- Last index: 600

In this case, since last index > `getLastCheckpointIndex()`, the transaction query just reverts.

## Recommendation
1. Ensure the array of request ids is sorted.
2. Use `getLastCheckpointIndex()` as the last index instead of `requestsToClaim.length + 1`.

### Balmy
Given the fact that Lido's request ids are incremental, and how we handle withdrawals in the adapter, I think it's safe to say that (1) will always be true, and request ids will be sorted. Applied recommendation (2) in PR 113.

### Cantina Managed
Fix looks good.
summary:
This bug report is about a code in LidoSTETHDelayedWithdrawalAdapter.sol file. The code is used to fetch a variable called "hints" using a specific function. However, there are some issues with the code that need to be fixed. 

The first requirement is that the array of request ids must be sorted. The second requirement is that the first index must be greater than 0, and the last index must be less than or equal to a specific value. However, the code is passing a value that is not equal to the specific value, which is causing problems. 

There are two cases that show the problems with the code. In the first case, if the length of the array is smaller than the specific value, then the hints will always be 0. In the second case, if the length of the array is larger than the specific value, then the transaction will fail. 

The recommendation to fix this bug is to ensure that the array of request ids is sorted and to use the specific value as the last index instead of the length of the array plus one. This recommendation has been applied in a pull request.

title: Complete loss event counter resets to 0 on partial loss
summary: This bug report is about a function in the YieldMath contract that is supposed to calculate updated yield and loss information. However, on a partial loss event, the function does not correctly update the complete loss event counter. This can affect calculations for yield and balance. The report includes a proof of concept and a recommendation for fixing the issue. The bug has been fixed in a pull request.

title: CompoundV2Connector#_convertSharesToAssets magnitude scalar can be too large and trun- cate the asset worth
summary:
This bug report is about a formula used in the CompoundV2Connector contract to calculate the worth of cTokens, which are tokens representing assets in the Compound protocol. The formula is supposed to take into account the number of decimals in the underlying asset, but it is currently off by 10^10. This means that the estimated worth of the asset is incorrect. 

To demonstrate the bug, a test was run using a fake user and the output showed that the redeemed DAI amount was off by 10 digits. The recommendation is to use 10^18 instead of 10^28 for the magnitude, as cTokens have 8 decimals. 

The bug has been fixed in a recent pull request and should also address another issue related to pending cToken interest.

title: Front-running exploit disrupts group IP management via derivative registration
summary: The bug report explains an issue with the GroupingModule function in the Group IP management system. This function allows users to register a new Group IP account and attach license terms to it. However, an attacker can front-run the owner's transaction and register a derivative IP, effectively locking the Group IP and preventing the owner from managing it. This creates a denial-of-service condition and disrupts the core functionality of the system. To fix this issue, a short time delay has been introduced to allow the owner to add new IPs without the risk of being front-run. The issue has been solved in the specified commit id by adding a new field called "disabled" to the LicensingConfig struct, which can be used by the owner to manage their group and revoke the disabled status when ready.

title: Griefing attack in group IP management via license token minting
summary:
The bug report describes an issue with the `registerGroup` function in the `GroupingModule` contract, which allows users to register a new Group IP account. The function calls another function, `registerGroup`, in the `GroupIPAssetRegistry` contract for the actual accounting process. 

After registering the Group IP, the owner should be able to attach license terms to it using the `attachLicenseTerms` function in the `LicensingModule` contract. However, there is no permission check to verify that the caller is authorized to mint license tokens for the Group IP. This means that any user can front-run the owner's transaction and mint license tokens without authorization. 

This bug can be exploited to prevent the legitimate owner from managing their Group IP, causing a denial-of-service condition. This disrupts the core functionality of the Group IP management system and can lead to operational and financial losses for the rightful owner. 

To fix this issue, it is recommended to implement strict access control in the `mintLicenseTokens` function to ensure that only the IP owner or authorized operators can mint license tokens for their IPs. This can be achieved by adding a `verifyPermission` modifier to the function. 

The issue has been resolved by adding a `disabled` field to the `LicensingConfig` struct, which can be set to `true` to prevent unauthorized minting of license tokens. This gives the Group IP owner control over their group and the ability to revoke the `disabled` status when ready to operate. 

The relevant code for this issue can be found in the `LicensingModule.sol` and `GroupingModule.sol` contracts.

title: Malicious IP owner can drain rewards via duplicate entries in claimReward function
summary: The RoyaltyModule is a system designed to distribute revenue fairly among members of a group. However, there is a vulnerability in the system that allows a malicious user to redirect all rewards to a single account within the group. This can be done by manipulating the reward distribution logic and passing the same IP Asset multiple times in the `ipIds` array when calling the `claimReward` function. This results in the IP Asset receiving a disproportionately large share of the rewards. To fix this issue, the uniqueness of IP Assets within the `ipIds` array should be enforced, and the vulnerability has been solved in the specified commit.

title: Denial of service caused by improper registration fee handling in group IP account
summary:
Summary:

The `registerGroup` function in the GroupingModule allows users to register a new Group IP account and calls the `registerGroup` function in the GroupIPAssetRegistry for the actual accounting process. However, there is a bug in the `_register` function, which is called internally, that does not properly handle the transfer of registration fees, causing the entire process to revert and breaking the core feature. This can be exploited to cause a denial of service. The bug has been fixed by passing the address of the user who intends to register the Group IP account and transferring fees from this address.

title: Incorrect Update Order in UpdateManager
description:
In the `UpdateManager contract`, the [`update function`](https://github.com/Fantom-foundation/Bridge/blob/558465d3aba2ffae1a4436a2fc14c723b82926df/contracts/UpdateManager.sol#L36) incorrectly calls `setValidators` on the previous `updateVerifier` instance instead of calling it on the newly updated one. This results in the new verifier contract being set without valid validators. Consequently, the `UpdateManager contract` could get bricked because when `verifyUpdate` is called on the new verifier, it would revert due to the absence of validators.


Consider setting the new verified address before calling `setValidators` to ensure that the correct instance is used.


***Update:** Resolved in [pull request \#62](https://github.com/Fantom-foundation/Bridge/pull/62).*
summary: The `UpdateManager contract` has a bug where the `update function` is not setting the correct validators on the new verifier contract, causing it to become unusable. This can cause issues with verifying updates and potentially "brick" the `UpdateManager contract`. The bug has been fixed in a recent pull request (#62) by setting the new verified address before calling `setValidators`.

title: TermMaxRouter::executeOperation() doesn't check if adapter is whitelisted before delegate- calling
summary: This bug report is about a vulnerability found in the `TermMaxRouter` contract. The `executeOperation()` function in the contract calls to an adapter which is controlled by anyone and can be used to rewrite the storage of the contract and perform any arbitrary operation. This can lead to the stealing of user funds. The likelihood of this attack is high as there are no constraints in performing it. The recommendation is to perform a check for whitelisted adapters before the first delegate call.

title: Rewards/Fees claimed by LPers are not removed from the market
summary: The bug report discusses an issue in the TermMax platform where rewards claimed by liquidity providers (LPers) are not removed from the total rewards. This leads to uneven distribution of rewards and can potentially result in a loss of funds for other LPers. The bug is caused by the fact that when an LPer withdraws liquidity, their LP tokens are burned but their claimed rewards are not, resulting in the total rewards remaining the same. The report includes a proof of concept and recommends burning the claimed rewards as well.

title: market.apr is calculated incorrectly for every swap 's execution
summary: This bug report is about a vulnerability in the TermMax protocol, which helps people lend and borrow money. The bug is in the code that calculates the interest rate borrowers pay. It is calculating the rate incorrectly, which can cause problems for both lenders and borrowers. This bug affects every function in the code, so it will happen every time someone uses the protocol. It is recommended to fix the code by using the correct values for the interest rate calculation. A proof of concept has been created to show the bug in action.

title: Anyone can call the ﬂashRepayFromColl function for any loan
summary: The report discusses a bug in a function called `flashRepay` that allows anyone to repay a loan using someone else's collateral. This can result in a loss of funds for the borrower, as well as potential loss of collateral. The report recommends that only the loan owner should be allowed to use this function.

title: LPs can split their liquidity withdrawal to get more tokens
summary: This bug report discusses an issue with LP rewards when withdrawing liquidity in multiple transactions. The formula used to calculate rewards is affected by a decrease in `lpSupply`, which can result in later LPs receiving more rewards than earlier ones. This can be exploited by malicious users, especially during high market activity. A proof of concept test case is provided to demonstrate the impact. The recommendation is to record `lpSupply` for each block and use the same value for all withdrawals in that block to prevent this issue.

title: Calling TermMaxMarket.setLsf leaks value to attackers via a sandwich attack
summary: This report discusses a vulnerability found in the TermMax protocol, specifically in their AMM (automated market maker) model. The issue stems from a function called `setLsf` which allows the market owner to modify the liquidity scaling factor (lsf) of the market. This factor affects the calculation of virtual reserves in the AMM, which can be exploited by attackers to manipulate the price of tokens and make a profit. This vulnerability has a high impact and medium likelihood, and the recommendation is for the protocol to remove the `setLsf` function and deploy multiple markets with different lsf values instead. The report includes two proof of concept test cases to demonstrate the exploit.

title: TermMaxMarket.provideLiquidity is vulnerable to donation attacks
summary: This report discusses a vulnerability found in the TermMax Market, which is a platform for exchanging custom tokens. The vulnerability allows attackers to steal funds from unsuspecting users who deposit their tokens into the market. The issue is caused by the use of manipulatable values in the market's liquidity addition process, which can be exploited to round down the amount of tokens minted for a victim to 0. This can result in the attacker stealing the victim's entire deposit. The severity of this issue is considered high, as it can lead to significant financial loss for the victim. The report recommends using an internal accounting system instead of relying on external values to prevent such attacks. A proof of concept is provided to demonstrate the validity of the finding.

title: Malicious users can steal swap fees from liquidity providers
summary:
Bug Summary: Malicious users can exploit a flaw in the swap process to deposit and remove liquidity in one transaction, stealing some LP rewards.

Impact: This bug can be used by malicious users to steal rewards from normal LP holders, causing them to lose some of their earnings.

Likelihood: This bug does not require any special conditions and can be easily exploited if there are accrued rewards.

Proof of Concept: A test case was added to demonstrate how the bug can be exploited, showing that the normal LP holder loses some rewards when a malicious user adds and removes liquidity before the normal user's removal.

Recommendation: The team should consider the actual active time of liquidity in the pool when calculating rewards to prevent this type of exploit.

title: LP Token Price Manipulation Through Reserve
summary: The BondSteerOracle contract has a flaw in its method of calculating the price of Steer Protocol LP tokens. The `_currentPrice` function uses spot reserves to determine the LP token value, which can be manipulated easily. This is because it does not take into account potential imbalances in the pool or market conditions, and there are no safeguards against extreme price movements or manipulation attempts. A proof of concept test has been provided to demonstrate how the price can be manipulated through reserve changes. The BVSS score for this vulnerability is 7.1, which is considered a medium risk. The recommended solution is to implement Alpha Finance's formula for pricing LP tokens, which calculates the price based on time-weighted average prices and the constant product invariant, providing resistance against manipulation attempts. The Lucid Labs team has already implemented this solution and an oracle implementation for the tokens prices of the LP Vault. The reference for this vulnerability is available on GitHub.

title: Mathematical Incompatibility Between FlexVotingClient and QuadraticVoteStrategy
summary: The report describes a problem that occurs when using a certain contract called FlexVotingClient with a specific voting strategy. The issue is caused by a conflict between two different calculations, which leads to transaction failures. This problem makes the system unusable and breaks the core functionality of the protocol. A test was conducted to demonstrate the issue, and a recommendation was made to create another contract or modify the existing one to solve the problem. The issue has been resolved by the Lucid Labs team by deciding not to use the FlexVotingClient with this specific strategy.

title: Bypass of Bridge Limits in burnAndBridgeMulti Function
summary: The AssetController contract allows users to bypass limits for individual bridges by using the burnAndBridgeMulti function. This is due to a lack of verification for duplicate adapter addresses, which can be exploited to exceed intended limits. A proof of concept test has been provided to demonstrate this vulnerability. It is recommended to implement a check for adapter uniqueness in the burnAndBridgeMulti function to prevent this exploit. The issue has been resolved by adding a new function to check for uniqueness.

title: Division by Zero in Quadratic Vote Weight Calculation
summary: The `QuadraticGitcoinPassportStrategy` contract has a bug that causes a division by zero error in its vote weight calculation. This happens when calculating the proportional match rate for Gitcoin Passport scores. This bug affects a significant portion of the scoring range and prevents users with scores in this range from casting votes. The recommended solution is to replace the current formula with a correct one. The issue has been solved by the Lucid Labs team by modifying the division by zero and adding checks in the constructor.

title: Lack of Access Control in receiveMessage in AssetController Contract
summary: This bug report is about a critical vulnerability found in the `AssetController.sol` contract. The `receiveMessage` function in this contract does not properly verify the identity of the caller, allowing anyone to call it directly and create or modify transfer records. This can lead to unauthorized token minting, theft of funds, or disruption of the entire cross-chain transfer system. A proof of concept test has been provided to demonstrate how an attacker can exploit this vulnerability. The BVSS score for this vulnerability is 10.0, indicating its severity. The recommended solution is to implement strict sender validation at the beginning of the `receiveMessage` function and to ensure that the `receivedTransfer.threshold` value is greater than 0.
