It has been fixed in the latest commit by calculating the minted amount based on the difference in account balance before and after the transfer.

title: LIQUIDITY POOL COULD RUN OUT OF SUSD TOKENS
description:
##### Description

When closing a position **long call**, the `_maybeExchangeBase` function is called with the argument `revertBuyOnInsufficientFunds` set to **false**. As a consequence, the liquidity pool will be able to swap sUSD for sETH without limits and could eventually run out of sUSD tokens.

This situation could affect some relevant operations such as withdrawal, premium payment, settlement, etc.

`Proof of Concept:`

Initial liquidity info for the test:

![](images/HAL-03/initial_situation.png)

The attacker opens a long call position of 120 sETH. There is a big difference between `lockedCollateral.base` and `sETH balance` because of \vulnref{DIFFERENCES BETWEEN LOCKED COLLATERAL AND SETH BALANCE ARE NOT ADEQUATELY CAPPED}:

![](images/HAL-03/open_position_1.png)
![](images/HAL-03/open_position_2.png)

Because of the difference, the owner decides to set `maxFeePaid` = **MAX\_UINT** to enable sETH repurchase.

On the other hand, a user withdraws sUSD from liquidity pool. The image shows liquidity info after withdrawal:

![](images/HAL-03/after_withdraw.png)

Finally, the attacker closes the 82.6 sETH long call position:

![](images/HAL-03/close_position_1.png)

Since the swap is not limited by any parameter, the protocol uses all available sUSD. In the end, the new sUSD balance is almost 0 (`0.29037...` in the example):

![](images/HAL-03/close_position_2.png)

Code Location
-------------

#### LiquidityPool.sol

```
(uint quoteSpent, uint baseReceived) = synthetixAdapter.exchangeToExactBaseWithLimit(
  exchangeParams,
  address(optionMarket),
  amountBase,
  revertBuyOnInsufficientFunds ? freeLiquidity : type(uint).max
);
emit BasePurchased(quoteSpent, baseReceived);

```

##### Score

Impact: 4  
Likelihood: 4

##### Recommendation

**SOLVED:** The issue was fixed in commit [d8d2e902c6d368313d9e04bec40c21fbf70b870b](https://github.com/lyra-finance/lyra-protocol/commit/d8d2e902c6d368313d9e04bec40c21fbf70b870b). With the update to the `_getLiquidity` function in the **LiquidityPool** contract, this attack vector is not feasible.
summary: The bug report describes a problem that occurs when closing a long call position. This causes the `_maybeExchangeBase` function to be called with the argument `revertBuyOnInsufficientFunds` set to false, which allows the liquidity pool to swap sUSD for sETH without limits. This can lead to the liquidity pool running out of sUSD tokens, affecting operations such as withdrawal, premium payment, and settlement. The report includes a proof of concept showing how an attacker can take advantage of this vulnerability. The bug has been fixed in a recent commit to the **LiquidityPool** contract.

title: COLLATERAL CAN BE UPDATED IN SETTLED BOARDS
summary: This bug report highlights an issue with the `_doTrade` and `addCollateral` functions in the **OptionMarket** contract. These functions allow for updating collateral on positions, even if the board is already settled. This can lead to unexpected situations such as added collateral getting stuck in the ShortCollateral contract, users negatively affecting the liquidity of the protocol, and collateral on positions being reduced to less than expected. The code locations for these functions are also provided for reference. The impact of this bug is rated as a 4 out of 5 and the likelihood is rated as a 5 out of 5. However, the issue has been solved with two recent commits to the code.

title: MISCALCULATION OF PENDING DELTA LIQUIDITY LEADS TO AN INCORRECT HEDGE
description:
##### Description

The `_getLiquidity` function in the **LiquidityPool** contract miscalculates the value of `pendingDeltaLiquidity` when **pendingDelta > freeLiquidity**.

Consequently, in the aforementioned situation, the liquidity pool cannot be used for withdrawals nor use the available liquidity for delta hedging, as shown in the following comparison table:

![](images/HAL-01/hedge.png)

`Scenario 2` shows that **pendingDeltaLiquidity**, the amount is used for delta hedging, could be up to 20 instead of just 5. This latter value is the incorrect amount proposed by `Scenario 1`.

Code Location
-------------

#### LiquidityPool.sol

```
uint usedQuote = totalOutstandingSettlements + totalQueuedDeposits + lockedCollateral.quote + pendingBaseValue;

uint totalQuote = quoteAsset.balanceOf(address(this));

liquidity.freeLiquidity = totalQuote > (usedQuote + reservedTokenValue)
  ? totalQuote - (usedQuote + reservedTokenValue)
  : 0;

// ensure pendingDelta <= liquidity.freeLiquidity
liquidity.pendingDeltaLiquidity = liquidity.freeLiquidity > pendingDelta ? pendingDelta : liquidity.freeLiquidity;
liquidity.freeLiquidity -= liquidity.pendingDeltaLiquidity;

liquidity.burnableLiquidity = totalQuote > (usedQuote + pendingDelta) ? totalQuote - (usedQuote + pendingDelta) : 0;

```

##### Score

Impact: 4  
Likelihood: 5

##### Recommendation

**SOLVED:** The issue was fixed in commit [d8d2e902c6d368313d9e04bec40c21fbf70b870b](https://github.com/lyra-finance/lyra-protocol/commit/d8d2e902c6d368313d9e04bec40c21fbf70b870b).
summary: The **LiquidityPool** contract has a bug in the `_getLiquidity` function which causes it to incorrectly calculate the value of `pendingDeltaLiquidity` when **pendingDelta** is greater than **freeLiquidity**. This results in the liquidity pool being unable to be used for withdrawals or delta hedging. The issue has been fixed in the code and the fix can be found in commit [d8d2e902c6d368313d9e04bec40c21fbf70b870b](https://github.com/lyra-finance/lyra-protocol/commit/d8d2e902c6d368313d9e04bec40c21fbf70b870b). The impact of this bug is rated as 4 out of 10 and the likelihood of it occurring is 5 out of 10.

title: DIFFERENCES BETWEEN LOCKED COLLATERAL AND SETH BALANCE ARE NOT ADEQUATELY CAPPED
summary: The bug report discusses a problem with the `lockedCollateral.base` and `sETH balance` in the liquidity pool for the Lyra protocol. This issue can cause distorted liquidity values, which can lead to various consequences such as running out of sUSD tokens, affecting operations like withdrawals and settlements, and making incorrect protocol decisions. The report provides a proof of concept and code location for the issue, along with a score and recommendation. The issue has been partially solved by a recent commit, but it is still recommended to keep an eye on it.

title: AUCTIONS AND BIDS COULD BE STUCK PERMANENTLY IN THE AUCTIONUPGRADEABLE CONTRACT IF A BID IS PLACED BY A BLACKLISTED USDC/USDT USER
description:
##### Description

The `AuctionUpgradeable` contract allows creating different auctions through the `createAuction()` function:

#### AuctionUpgradeable.sol

```
function createAuction(
    uint96 startTime,
    uint96 duration,
    address sellToken,
    uint256 trancheIndex,
    uint128 sellAmount,
    uint128 minBidAmount,
    uint128 fixedPrice,
    uint128 priceRangeStart,
    uint128 priceRangeEnd,
    AuctionType auctionType
) external payable returns (uint256)

```

Once an auction is completed, the `closeAuction()` function will be called and will distribute the `sellToken` between all the bidders. As currently USDC contains a blacklist of users which cannot transfer or receive this token, the following issue could occur:

1. Alice creates an auction of 1000 USDC(`sellToken`).
2. Users place different bids for the USDC auction.
3. A Blacklisted USDC user also places a bid for the USDC auction. The bid is placed using a whitelisted `purchaseToken` like DAI.
4. The auction is completed. `closeAuction()` is called, but it reverts every time as the USDC transfer to the blacklisted USDC user is forbidden.
5. The auction USDC `sellTokens` are now stuck in the contract. All the bids are also stuck permanently in the contract.
6. Similar issue can occur with USDT as it also contains a blacklist of users.

![poc4.png](https://halbornmainframe.com/proxy/audits/images/659f0a4ca1aa3698c0f2b6be)

##### BVSS

[AO:A/AC:L/AX:L/C:N/I:N/A:N/D:C/Y:N/R:N/S:U (10.0)](/bvss?q=AO:A/AC:L/AX:L/C:N/I:N/A:N/D:C/Y:N/R:N/S:U)

##### Recommendation

**SOLVED:** The `Irrigation Protocol team` solved the issue by enforcing a whitelist on the `sellTokens`. The whitelist will not include blacklistable tokens like USDC/USDT.

`Commit ID :` [cae1d1718ef504f4fc27ba1aa464600a71ae635a](https://github.com/IrrigationProtocol/irrigation-contracts-diamond/commit/cae1d1718ef504f4fc27ba1aa464600a71ae635a).
summary: The `AuctionUpgradeable` contract has a bug that can cause USDC or USDT tokens to become stuck in the contract. This happens when a blacklisted user bids on an auction using a whitelisted token. The contract does not allow transfers to blacklisted users, so the auction cannot be closed and the tokens become stuck. The Irrigation Protocol team has solved this issue by enforcing a whitelist on the `sellTokens` and the bug has been fixed in commit ID cae1d1718ef504f4fc27ba1aa464600a71ae635a.

title: SPRINKLERUPGRADEABLE CONTRACT CAN BE DRAINED THROUGH THE EXCHANGETOWATER FUNCTION
summary: The report describes a bug in the `SprinklerUpgradeable` contract, where a malicious user can drain all the WATER tokens from the contract by calling the `exchangeTokenToWater` function with a high amount of Native Ether. This is possible because the contract does not check if the token address is actually a smart contract with code deployed in it. The recommended solution was to implement a check for the token address using the `SafeERC20` library. The Irrigation Protocol team has solved the issue by implementing the recommended solution in commit ID 2a75e858618864b3962c623035cca5b5aef4ff4d.

title: INITIAL LP DEPOSIT IS IMPOSSIBLE DUE TO MISCALCULATION
summary: The `_depositNoPull()` function in the `BaseStrategy` contract is not working properly. When the value of the `s.BORROWED_INVARIANT` variable is zero, the contract still tries to mint LP tokens to developers, resulting in a `ZeroAmount()` error and preventing users from depositing funds. A proof of concept has been provided to demonstrate this issue. The code responsible for this bug has been identified and a solution has been implemented in the codebase. The fix can be found in the `v1-strategies::6f6a7ba1f0fe8b9d7a7cb9b756ef5b3e6bfa55ab` commit. The impact of this bug is rated as 3 out of 5 and the likelihood of encountering it is 5 out of 5. It is recommended to update the code by replacing the `greater than or equal to (>=)` relation with `greater than (>)` relation to solve this issue.

title: BRIDGENFT CALL CAN BE FRONTRUN
summary: The NFTMintingBridge contract has a function called bridgeNft() which is used to transfer ERC721 tokens from one chain to another. However, there is a bug in this function where it does not check if the caller actually owns the token they are trying to transfer. This allows for a potential attack where a malicious user can front-run the transaction and steal the token. The Gains Trade team has fixed this issue by adding a requirement that the caller must be the owner of the token.

title: COVER MAY BE UPDATED FOR MONTH'S VALUES OUT OF RANGE
summary: This bug report discusses an issue with a function in the PriorityPool contract where a new deadline update may result in a month value that is out of range. This can lead to new covers not being obtained and affecting the functionality of the contract. The code location is provided and a screenshot of the issue is included. The impact and likelihood of the bug are rated as 4 out of 5 and a recommendation to solve the issue is also provided. The bug has now been solved by adjusting the `_updateCoverInfo` function to consider elapsed time between years.

title: MINTING ZERO AMOUNT DEADLOCK IS PRODUCED DURING PAYOUT CLAIMING
summary: The bug report discusses an issue with the `newPayout` function in the `PayoutPool` smart contract. This function is used to calculate a payout and one of the parameters used is `payout.ratio`. However, when `payout.ratio` is equal to the constant `SCALE`, the function always reverts. This is because the variables `claimableBalance` and `claimable` become equal, resulting in the `newGenerationCRAmount` variable being set to `0`. This variable is used to specify the number of tokens to mint in the next generation, hence the function always fails at this point. The impact and likelihood of this bug are both rated as 4 out of 5. The recommendation is to fix the `claimPayout` function to prevent it from minting `0` tokens.

title: INVALID REWARD UPDATING MECHANISM
summary: This bug report is about a problem with the `_updateReward` function in the `WeightedFarmingPool.sol` file. When multiple months have passed, the function does not work properly. This is because it does not take into account if the current year and last year are different, which can cause the `for` loop to only iterate over a maximum of 12 months and sometimes not iterate at all. Additionally, there are issues with using the `_getDaysInMonth` function and calculating the reward for the first and last months. The impact of this bug is rated as 4 out of 5 and the likelihood of it occurring is rated as 5 out of 5. The recommendation is to solve these issues by implementing the recommended fixes. This bug has now been solved.

title: BUYING COVER FOR THREE MONTHS IS NEVER COUNTED DURING THE CURRENT MONTH
summary: The bug report describes an issue with the function `_updateCoverInfo` in the target pool. This function is responsible for storing the covered amount per month when a cover is bought. However, when trying to cover an amount for three months, the value is only stored in the index `currentMonth + 3` of `currentYear`. This causes a problem when the function `activeCovered` tries to retrieve the active cover amount, as it only iterates over the `coverInMonth` array starting from `currentMonth` as index `0` and never reaches the third month due to the loop condition being `i < 3`. This bug has a high impact and a high likelihood of occurring. The recommended solution is to update the code so that `_updateCoverInfo` stores the cover information in the correct year and month indexes. This issue has now been solved.

title: UPDATE REWARDS MAY CAUSE A DENIAL OF SERVICE BETWEEN YEARS
summary: The bug report describes an issue where the calculation of the difference in months between reward updates does not take into account changes in years. This can result in an integer overflow and cause incorrect calculations. The bug is located in two different files, `WeightedFarmingPool.sol` and `ProtectionPool.sol`. The impact of this bug is rated as 4 out of 5 and the likelihood of it occurring is 5 out of 5. The recommendation is to solve the issue by considering elapsed years between executions and removing the function in `ProtectionPool.sol` where the bug was found.

title: UNABLE TO CLAIM PAYOUTS
summary:
This bug report is about a potential issue with two functions, `getExcludedCoverageOf` and `getClaimableOf`, in the `CoverRightToken` smart contract. The problem arises when the `voteTimestamp` value is used without checking if the last incident is in the voting state or not. This can cause the `_getEOD` function to underflow and return a value of 0. This can also happen when someone creates a report using the `report` function, which adds the report to the `poolReports` array and sets the `voteTimestamp` to 0. The only time this is allowed is when the report voting is successful.

This issue prevents users from claiming their payout in the `PayoutPool` for a report that has already been voted on and has a corresponding `crToken`. The code that needs to be fixed is located in the `CoverRightToken.sol` file, specifically in the `getExcludedCoverageOf` function. The impact of this bug is rated as 5 out of 10 and the likelihood of it occurring is 3 out of 10.

The recommended solution to this bug is to check for valid reports based on their generation, meaning that only reports with a result of `SUCCESS` will be counted. This has been implemented and the bug has been solved.

title: INVALID PERCENTAGE RESULTS IN LESS PAYED DEBT
summary: The `payDebt` function in the `IncidentReport` section of the code is not working properly. It is using the wrong value to calculate debt percentages. The code states that the `DEBT_RATIO` is 80%, but it is actually using 0.8%. This is causing issues with the function. This bug has a medium impact and a low likelihood of occurring. The recommended solution is to change the calculation to use a maximum ratio of 100:1 between the two values.

title: REPORTING DEADLOCK IF QUORUM NOT REACHED
summary: The `settle` function in the `IncidentReport` code does not properly reset the `reported` state when the required number of votes is not reached. This means that the contract will not accept any new reports for the same `poolId` in the future. To fix this, a new function called `_setReportedStatus` has been added to properly reset the report status when the quorum is not reached. This bug has a medium impact and a low likelihood of occurring.

title: INVALID EXTERNAL CALL DOES CAUSE CONTRACT DEADLOCK
summary: This bug report is about a problem that occurs when trying to claim payouts. The issue is that when the `claim` function is executed in the `PayoutPool` smart contract, it always reverts. This is because the `burn` function, which is called in the `claim` function, can only be executed by the `PolicyCenter` smart contract. This means that any other smart contract trying to execute the `burn` function will be denied access and the `claim` function will fail. The code locations for the affected functions are provided in the report. The impact and likelihood of this issue are both rated as 5, indicating a high severity bug. The recommendation for solving this issue is to add a modifier to the `CoverRightToken` smart contract to allow calls from both the `PolicyCenter` and `PayoutPool` smart contracts. This bug has been marked as solved.

title: INVALID VARIABLE VISIBILITY DOES CAUSE CONTRACT DEADLOCK
summary: The bug report describes an issue with the `dynamicPremiumRatio` function in the `PriorityPool` contract. When this function is executed 7 days after the pool is deployed, it tries to retrieve a variable called `dynamicPoolCounter` from the `PriorityPoolFactory` contract. However, since this variable is marked as `internal`, the function always reverts at this point. This means that the function cannot be successfully executed. This bug has a high impact and likelihood of occurring. The recommendation is to make the `dynamicPoolCounter` variable `public` so that it can be accessed externally and solve the issue.

title: POOL INCOMES ON REPORTER REWARD CAN BE ARBITRARILY INCREASED
description:
##### Description

The function `premiumIncome` allows increasing arbitrarily the array of pool incomes used to calculate the final reward for a correct reporter. Using this function to increase the value of a selected pool income before executing an incident report made from a malicious account could lead to an attacker draining the entire `SHD` token balance from `Treasury` smart contract.

Code Location
-------------

#### src/pools/Treasury.sol

```
function premiumIncome(uint256 _poolId, uint256 _amount) external {
    poolIncome[_poolId] += _amount;
}

```

![token_drainage.png](https://halbornmainframe.com/proxy/audits/images/659ea547a1aa3698c0ebdb74)

##### Score

Impact: 5  
Likelihood: 5

##### Recommendation

**SOLVED**: The code is now checking that the caller is only the `policyCenter`.
summary: The `premiumIncome` function in the `Treasury.sol` file has a bug that allows attackers to steal all the `SHD` tokens from the `Treasury` smart contract. This can happen if the function is used to increase the value of a selected pool income before a malicious account executes an incident report. The impact and likelihood of this bug are both rated as 5 out of 5. The recommended solution is to update the code to check that only the `policyCenter` can call the function. This issue has been resolved.

title: DEPOSITING TO SECONDARY TOKENS DOES CAUSE THE CONTRACT TO LOCK
summary:
The bug report describes an issue with the code in the WeightedFarmingPool.sol file. The code is assuming that the user's amount will contain an array for all newly added tokens to the pool. However, this is not always the case when a user makes their first deposit on a token with an index that is not equal to zero. This can cause problems with the calculations and potentially lead to incorrect results. The bug has been given a score of 5 for both impact and likelihood, meaning it is a significant issue that is likely to occur. 

The recommended solution for this bug is to check the length of the user's amount array and compare it to the index. If there is a difference, empty values will be pushed to ensure that the arrays are the same length. This will prevent any errors from occurring and ensure that the calculations are accurate.

title: PUBLICLY EXPOSED FUNCTIONS
description:
##### Description

Several functions are being involved in the management of the `WeightedFarmingPool` contract, which are publicly exposed and without any sort of access control:

* `addPool`: It can add an arbitrary pool into the system.
* `addToken`: It can add any token, even not whitelisted, into any pool.
* `updateWeight`: It does allow updating the weight of any token of any pool.
* `setWeight`: Same as `updateWeight` but for the entire pool tokens.
* `updateRewardSpeed`: It does allow updating the rewards per second for a pool.
* `setPolicyCenter`: as described on "DEPOSITING TO ANY POOL/TOKEN WITH ANY AMOUNT VIA CONTROLLED POLICY CENTER".

Code Location
-------------

#### src/reward/WeightedFarmingPool.sol

```
function updateWeight(
    uint256 _id,
    address _token,
    uint256 _newWeight
) external {
    updatePool(_id);

    uint256 index = _getIndex(_id, _token);

    pools[_id].weight[index] = _newWeight;
}

```

##### Score

Impact: 5  
Likelihood: 5

##### Recommendation

**SOLVED**: All the stated calls are checking if the sender is a valid-registered pool using `IPriorityPoolFactory`. The `setPolicyCenter` function was removed from the `WeightedFarmingPool` contract.
summary: In the WeightedFarmingPool contract, there are several functions that can be accessed by anyone without any restrictions. These functions include adding a pool, adding a token (even if it's not whitelisted), updating the weight of a token, setting the weight for all tokens in a pool, and updating the rewards per second for a pool. This can lead to potential security risks. The code for these functions can be found in the WeightedFarmingPool.sol file. The impact of this bug is rated as 5 out of 10 and the likelihood of it occurring is also rated as 5 out of 10. The recommendation for solving this issue is to remove the setPolicyCenter function from the WeightedFarmingPool contract and to check if the sender is a valid-registered pool using IPriorityPoolFactory.

title: UPDATING THE 0 INDEX TOKEN WEIGHT VIA UNREGISTERED TOKENS
summary: The `updateWeight` function in the `WeightedFarmingPool.sol` file is not working properly. It is using an incorrect index to update the pool weight, which can result in the wrong token weight being updated. Additionally, the code does not check if the weight being updated is greater than 0. This can cause issues with the pool's functionality. The impact and likelihood of this bug are both rated as 5, meaning it is a high priority issue. The recommendation is to use a new mapping called `supported` to keep track of supported tokens instead of relying on arrays. This will solve the problem.

title: AN ATTACKER CAN WITHDRAW NOT OWNED TOKENS AND STEAL FUNDS
summary: The `_withdraw` function in the `WeightedFarmingPool.sol` file is using an incorrect function called `_getIndex` which is causing transfers to take place into any token specified by the user instead of the intended token. This can potentially lead to loss of funds for the user. The impact and likelihood of this bug are both rated as 5 out of 10. The recommendation is to replace the current method with a new mapping to keep track of supported tokens for a given pool. This issue has been resolved.

title: DEPOSITING ON ANY POOL USING ANY TOKEN
summary: The bug report describes an issue with the `deposit` function in the `WeightedFarmingPool` contract. This function does not properly check the token being used and can lead to malicious tokens being used to increase the stacked amount of the first pool token. This is due to the `_getIndex` function returning a value of `0` when a token is not found, causing the first token of the pool to be used and the balance to be incremented. This can be exploited by a malicious user to increase their rewards without actually transferring any tokens. The impact and likelihood of this bug are both rated as 5 out of 10. The recommended solution is to use a new mapping to keep track of supported tokens for a given pool id instead of relying on arrays. This issue has been solved in the code.

title: CODE NOT CHECKING IF TOKEN IS NOT PRESENT
summary: The code for `_getIndex` function in `WeightedFarmingPool` does not include a check to see if the token exists in the pool. This means that if the token is not found, the function will return index `0` by default, causing the token to be treated as part of the pool even if it is not. This could lead to errors in the pool's calculations and rewards. The code can be found in `src/reward/WeightedFarmingPool.sol`. This bug has a high impact and likelihood of occurring. The recommendation is to update the code by introducing a new mapping to keep track of supported tokens for a given pool id. This issue has been solved.

title: DEPOSITING TO ANY POOL/TOKEN WITH ANY AMOUNT VIA CONTROLLED POLICY CENTER
summary: This bug report is about a function called `setPolicyCenter` that is used to modify a variable called `policyCenter` in a smart contract. This variable is used to verify if the caller of certain functions is allowed to access them. However, the function does not have any access control, which means that anyone can change the value of `policyCenter`. This allows an attacker to manipulate the system by adding pool liquidity without owning any tokens. The impact and likelihood of this bug are both rated as 5, meaning it is a serious issue. The recommendation is to solve this problem by implementing access control modifiers.

title: CANNOT LIQUIDATE LIQUIDATABLE SECUREDLOAN DUE TO COLLATERAL RATIO CHECK
summary: The `SecuredLoan` contract has a function called `liquidate()` which allows the arbiter to take control of the collateral and repay the debt for the lender. However, there is a bug where the arbiter is unable to liquidate the collateral in some cases. This happens when the loan's deadline has passed and the collateral ratio is below the threshold. The reason for this is that the `liquidate()` function has an assertion that checks if the collateral ratio is below the threshold, but the ratio can take time to decrease while the loan's interest increases. This bug has been fixed by the `Debt DAO team` in a recent update, allowing the `liquidate()` function to be called regardless of the collateral ratio.

summary: This bug report describes an issue with the `EscrowedLoan` contract where the `_healthcheck()` function does not correctly set the loan's status to `LIQUIDATABLE` when the collateral ratio is incorrect. This can lead to the contract being in a `LIQUIDATABLE` state, allowing unauthorized functions to be called, which can result in the contract being in a malformed state. The borrower can potentially fix this by adding more collateral and repeatedly calling the `healthcheck()` function. The report also includes steps to reproduce the issue and a recommendation from the `Debt DAO` to accept the risk.

title: DOUBLE UPDATE OF UNUSEDTOKENS COLLECTION POSSIBLE
summary: This bug report describes an issue in the `SpigotedLoan` contract where adding a new revenue contract that earns in `credit tokens` can cause the `unusedTokens` collection to be updated twice, resulting in locked tokens. This can be triggered by calling the `claimAndTrade()` function, which updates the collection with target tokens (credit tokens) that were traded. The project team has confirmed this scenario, and it affects the `sweep()` function, which reverts due to an incorrect balance in the collection. The issue has been resolved in commit [760c5bfb9c352fb681f8351253ff9776b176e357](https://github.com/debtdao/smart-contracts/commit/760c5bfb9c352fb681f8351253ff9776b176e357) by updating the `unusedTokens` collection only once. The impact and likelihood of this issue are both rated as 4, and the Debt DAO team has solved it.

title: UNUSED REVENUE TOKENS LOCKOUT WHILE LOAN IS ACTIVE
summary: This bug report is about a vulnerability found in the `SpigotedLoan` contract. This contract allows borrowers to add spigots with revenue contracts that will help repay their debt. However, the `claimAndRepay()` and `claimAndTrade()` functions have a bug that allows for trading fewer revenue tokens than previously claimed. The remaining tokens are locked in the contract until the debt is paid off through other means. This vulnerability can be exploited by borrowers to use fewer tokens to pay off their debt, making the revenue split mechanism ineffective. The bug has been solved by the `Debt DAO team` in their latest commit, which now allows for trading unused revenue tokens to pay off debt.

title: PAYING OFF DEBT WITH SPIGOT EARNING IN ETHER IS NOT POSSIBLE
summary: This report discusses a bug in the `SpigotedLoan` contract where claiming and trading ether from a spigot is not possible. This is due to the internal function `_claimAndTrade()` assuming that the revenue token is an ERC20 token in every case, which is not the case for ether. This means that the escrowed ether remains locked until the debt is paid off through other means. The report includes steps to reproduce the bug and provides a solution that has been implemented by the Debt DAO team. The impact and likelihood of this bug are rated as 4 and 5 respectively.

title: BORROWING FROM NON-FIRST POSITION CAN DEADLOCK CONTRACT
summary: This bug report describes an issue in the `LineOfCredit` contract where a borrower can borrow from multiple lenders but can only repay the first credit position using specific functions. However, if the borrower borrows from a non-first position, they are unable to repay the debt or close the credit position due to a modifier that blocks the operation. This can lead to a deadlock situation where the borrower is unable to pay off the debt. The root cause of this issue is a function that does not properly update the position of the borrowed credit. The recommended solution is to update the function to properly shift the credit position to the beginning of the collection. This issue has been solved by the Debt DAO team in a recent commit.

title: UPDATEOWNERSPLIT FUNCTION CAN BE ABUSED BY LENDER OR BORROWER
summary: The `SpigotedLoan` contract has a bug where the `updateOwnerSplit()` function can be abused by the borrower or lender to change the percentage of revenue used to pay off the debt. This can happen if the `ownerSplit` parameter is set below or above the `defaultRevenueSplit` parameter. The function is also meant to be called by the arbiter or borrower, but there is no authorization check. The risk of this bug has been accepted by the Debt DAO team, but it is recommended to always use default values.

title: GETOUTSTANDINGDEBT FUNCTION RETURNS UNDERSTATED VALUE
summary: Summary: The `getOutstandingDebt()` function in the `LineOfCredit` contract does not accurately calculate the total outstanding debt, as it does not consider accrued interest from previous evaluation periods. This results in a misleading and understated value for users. The bug has been solved by replacing the `getOutstandingDebt()` function with the `updateOutstandingDebt()` function, which includes both updated principal and accrued interest.

title: COLLATERAL TOKENS LOCKOUT IN ESCROW
summary: This bug report discusses an issue with the `releaseCollateral()` function in the `Escrow` contract. This function is used by borrowers to withdraw their collateral, but it was found that when the last part of the collateral is released, the function updates the collateral amount to 0, making it impossible for borrowers to withdraw the remaining collateral. This is because the function checks the collateral ratio, which is always 0 in this case, making the assertion `cratio >= minimumCollateralRatio` always false. This issue was found during testing, where a borrower was unable to withdraw their remaining collateral. The impact and likelihood of this bug were rated as 5 out of 5, indicating a high risk. The recommendation for this issue was to check the loan status against the `REPAID` value, which has since been implemented in the code. The issue has been resolved in the latest commit by the `Debt DAO team`.

summary:
The LineOfCredit contract has a function called `withdraw()` which allows the lender to take back any unused deposits. However, if the lender withdraws all deposits before the borrower has borrowed any money, it can cause the contract to become stuck. This is because the `withdraw()` function also calls another function called `_accrueInterest()` which can cause a small amount of interest to be accrued. This can prevent the borrower from paying off their debt or closing the credit.

The bug was found in the `whileBorrowing()` modifier which is used in both the LineOfCredit and SpigotedLoan contracts. This modifier checks if any principal has been borrowed, but it does not check if any interest has been accrued. This can lead to the contract becoming stuck if all deposits are withdrawn before any borrowing has occurred.

To exploit this bug, a user would need to follow these steps:
1. Deploy and initialize all necessary contracts.
2. Add a credit position for 1,000,000,000,000,000 tokens as both the borrower and lender.
3. As the lender, use the `withdraw()` function to take back all deposits.
4. As the borrower, try to use the `depositAndClose()` function, which will fail.
5. Then try to close the credit, which will also fail.
6. Finally, try to borrow the deposit, which will fail.

The impact of this bug is rated as 5 out of 10 and the likelihood of it occurring is also rated as 5 out of 10. The recommendation to fix this bug is to update the `_close()` internal function to only check that the principal is not zero before closing, instead of also checking the interest accrued parameter. This issue has been solved in commit b30347d17a90980aa7ca7c0ffb25067f87039c6d by the Debt DAO team.

title: ORACLE PRICE AFFECTS THE POSSIBILITY OF DEBT REPAYMENT
summary: The LineOfCredit contract has a bug that affects the `interestUsd` parameter. This parameter is used to track unpaid interest in USD. The bug occurs in the `_accrueInterest()` and `_repay()` functions. The `_accrueInterest()` function is used by several other functions, including `accrueInterest()` and `setRates()`, while the `_repay()` function is used by `depositAndRepay()` and `depositAndClose()`. The `interestUsd` parameter is strongly affected by the price returned by the Oracle. If the Oracle returns a higher value than before, an integer underflow occurs in the `_repay()` function, making debt repayment impossible. To exploit this vulnerability, `_accrueInterest()` must be called before `_repay()` to update the `interestUsd` parameter. The codebase uses the `SimpleOracle` mock for testing, and the `ChangingOracle` was created to mimic a price increase after ten days. To exploit this vulnerability, all necessary contracts must be deployed and initialized, and then the borrower must add a credit position for 1,000,000,000,000,000 tokens. After that, the borrower must borrow 1,000,000,000,000,000 tokens, and then forward the blockchain time for 10 days. The borrower must then call the `accrueInterest()` function to update the `interestUsd` parameter. Finally, the borrower must forward the blockchain time for one more day and attempt to call the `depositAndClose()` function, which will result in a transaction revert due to an integer overflow. This bug was solved by the Debt DAO team in the commit 51dab65755c9978333b147f99db007a93bd0f81c and cbb2f0f2b68b966e95d2d64a2686de33f4c0496b by removing the `interestUsd` parameter and related calculations. The likelihood and impact of this bug are both rated as 5, and the Debt DAO team has recommended that this bug be solved.

title: LENDER CAN WITHDRAW INTEREST MULTIPLE TIMES
description:
##### Description

In the `LineOfCredit` contract, a lender has the possibility to withdraw accrued interest via `withdrawInterest()` function. The function does not record the fact of withdrawal; thus, the function can be called multiple times until the contract has a positive token balance. `LineOfCredit``withdrawInterest()`

As a result, in the case of multiple lenders recorded in the contract, one lender can extract liquidity from other lenders.
Alternatively, a lender can pull unborrowed deposits and force borrowers to pay off higher debt than expected, or force default.

#### LineOfCredit.sol

```
    function withdrawInterest(bytes32 id)
        external
        override
        returns (uint256)
    {
        require(
            msg.sender == credits[id].lender,
            "Loan: only lender can withdraw"
        );

        _accrueInterest(id);

        uint256 amount = credits[id].interestAccrued;
```

summary: The `LineOfCredit` contract has a function called `withdrawInterest()` that allows a lender to withdraw accrued interest. However, this function does not record the fact of withdrawal, allowing the lender to call it multiple times until the contract has a positive token balance. This can lead to one lender taking liquidity from other lenders or forcing borrowers to pay off higher debt than expected, potentially resulting in default. This bug has been demonstrated in two scenarios, one where a lender steals other lenders' liquidity and another where a lender steals borrower liquidity. The impact and likelihood of this bug are both rated as 5 out of 5. The recommendation is to remove the `withdrawInterest()` function from the contract, which has been done in a recent commit by the `Debt DAO team`.

title: DEBT PAY OFF IMPOSSIBLE DUE TO INTEGER UNDERFLOW
summary: This bug report is about a bug found in the `LineOfCredit` contract. The bug causes both the `depositAndClose()` and `depositAndRepay()` functions to fail due to integer overflow. This happens because the `principalUsd` parameter is not properly updated in the `_createCredit` function, resulting in a value of 0. This bug can be exploited by a borrower to avoid paying off their debt. The impact and likelihood of this bug are both rated as 5. The recommendation is to remove the `principalUsd` parameter and related calculations to solve the issue. This has been resolved in commit [51dab65755c9978333b147f99db007a93bd0f81c](https://github.com/debtdao/smart-contracts/commit/51dab65755c9978333b147f99db007a93bd0f81c) by the Debt DAO team.

title: LENDER LIQUIDITY LOCKOUT POSSIBLE VIA DEPOSITANDCLOSE FUNCTION
summary: The `LineOfCredit` contract has a bug that affects the lender's liquidity. When the borrower uses the `depositAndClose()` function to repay their debt, the lender's funds are not transferred back to them. This means that the lender's liquidity is locked in the contract. The bug is caused by the internal `_close` function, which deletes the debt record without transferring the lender's funds. This can be exploited by the borrower, as they can close the debt without returning the lender's funds. The bug has been fixed by the `Debt DAO team` in their latest commit, where the transfer of the lender's liquidity now happens on the `_close()` function. This issue has a high impact and likelihood, and it is recommended to update the contract to the latest version to avoid this bug.

title: PARTIAL MATCH CAN LEAD TO UNDERFLOW LOCKING USER FUNDS
summary: The bug report describes an issue with a function called `matchIn()` and `matchOut()` in a contract called `Passage.sol`. These functions are meant to match orders and reduce the counters for the number of fully matched orders. However, the counters are being increased even when there is a partial match, leading to incorrect counter values and causing other functions to fail. This can result in users being unable to cancel their orders or match new orders, leading to a denial of service. The report also includes a code snippet and a proof of concept of the issue. The report has been assigned a BVSS score of 10.0, indicating a critical vulnerability. The recommendation is to fix the issue by checking that the available ether is equal to the amount being matched before increasing the counter. The issue has been solved by the client team in a commit with the code.

title: PERFECTLY MATCHING AN ORDER AND THEN CANCELING CAN LEAD TO THE POINTER BEING 0 WITH REMAINING ORDERS
summary: The report describes a bug where it is possible to set certain variables to 0 in a smart contract called Passage.sol. This can happen when a user cancels an order and then calls a function called `autoMatch` again. This can lead to users having their funds locked and transactions not being able to go through. The report also provides an example of how this bug can occur and the severity of the issue. The team responsible for the smart contract has fixed the issue in a recent commit.

title: MATCHING AN ORDER WITH NO NEXT NODE IN THE LINKEDLIST CAN CAUSE A DENIAL OF SERVICE OF THE CONTRACT
summary: The `Passage` contract has a bug where after a match, the pointers for matching orders can point to an order with 0 available ether, causing a denial-of-service and locking up funds. This can happen when an order is cancelled, reducing the available ether of the next order to 0. The bug has been fixed by the development team.

title: CANCELLING THE INVESTMENT IN THE POINTER CAN LOCK THE FUNDS FROM OTHER USERS
summary: The `Passage` contract has a bug that causes orders to not be properly matched or cancelled. This happens because the `autoMatch()` function, which matches orders, relies on `inPtr` and `outPtr` variables to keep track of the first non-matched orders. However, when an order is cancelled, these pointers are not properly recalculated, causing them to point to already-matched orders or become 0. This means that subsequent orders cannot be cancelled or matched, and funds cannot be withdrawn. The bug has been fixed by the \client team in commit [ca7bd2b1](https://gitlab.com/bracketlabs/bracketx-halborn/-/commit/ca7bd2b1fcb48baf7fc5151762772e32335667b4).

title: RE-ENTRANCY WHEN MINTING LP TOKENS CAN LEAD TO STEALING VAULT FUNDS
summary: The BPLP contract uses ERC1155 tokens to keep track of tokens based on the vault id. However, there is a vulnerability in the code that allows for re-entrancy attacks, where an attacker can exploit the deposit function to mint extra shares and steal funds from other users. This can happen because the `amtETH` variable used in the token calculation formula is updated after minting, making it lower than it should be in the case of re-entrancy. A proof of concept has been provided, where Alice deposits 10 ether and receives 10ˆ18 shares, but Bob exploits the vulnerability and receives 25 ether while Alice only receives 15 ether. The BVSS score for this vulnerability is 10.0, and the recommended solution is to add the `nonReentrant` modifier to the `deposit()` function. This issue has been solved by the client team in commit [78f58a33](https://gitlab.com/bracketlabs/bracketx-halborn/-/commit/78f58a337fa0ad0b318960ea10e3846bd6082e04).

title: ALL THE FUNDS FROM THE VAULTS CAN BE STOLEN BY FRONT-RUNNING DEPOSIT FUNCTION
summary: The BPLP contract is used for automatic trading in the Passage contract by creating vaults where users can lock their funds for a specified time. After the policies are claimed, users can withdraw their earnings based on the number of shares they have. However, a bug was found where an attacker could front-run transactions and steal all the funds in the vault. This was due to the way shares were calculated, allowing an attacker to deposit a small amount and manipulate the share calculation to their advantage. The bug has been fixed by preventing users from using the credit() function until the vault is closed.

title: VULNERABLE ECDSA LIBRARY
description:
##### Description

A vulnerability found in the `ECDSA` library developed by the OpenZeppelin team. OpenZeppelin team published a security advisory on GitHub on August 22nd, 2022. According to the vulnerability, `recover` and `tryRecover` functions are vulnerable, as those functions accept the standard signature format and compact signature format. (EIP-2098)

The functions ECDSA.recover and ECDSA.tryRecover are vulnerable to some sort of signature malleability because they accept compact EIP-2098 signatures in addition to the traditional 65-byte signature format.
This is only an issue for the functions that take a single byte argument, and not the functions that take r, v, s or r, vs as separate arguments.

Potentially affected contracts are those that implement signature reuse or replay protection by marking the signature itself as used, rather than the signed message or a nonce included in it. A user can take a signature that has already been submitted, submit it again in a different form, and bypass this protection.

It was observed that Biconomy contracts were using the vulnerable `ECDSA` library to recover signatures.

[ECDSA Signature Malleability](https://github.com/OpenZeppelin/openzeppelin-contracts/security/advisories/GHSA-4h98-2769-gh6h)

Code Location
-------------

#### package.json

```
"@openzeppelin/contracts": "^4.2.0",
"@openzeppelin/contracts-upgradeable": "^4.7.3",

```

The PoC code below proofs that both signatures addresses the same address, as they are identical but in different formats.

#### ECDSA vulnerability test case - PoC

```
function testValidateUserOpPaymaster() public {

        UserOperation memory userOp = UserOperation({
            sender: user1,
            nonce: 0,
            initCode:  new bytes(0x0),
            callData:  new bytes(0x0),
            callGasLimit: 0,
            verificationGasLimit: 0,
            preVerificationGas: 0,
            maxFeePerGas: 0,
            maxPriorityFeePerGas: 0,
            paymasterAndData: new bytes(0x0),
            signature: new bytes(0x0)
        });

        bytes32 hash = paymentMasterNew.getHash(userOp);

        (uint8 v, bytes32 r, bytes32 s) = vm.sign(101, hash.toEthSignedMessageHash());
        bytes memory signature = abi.encodePacked(r, s, v);
        bytes memory paymasterAndData = abi.encodePacked(user1, signature);

        userOp.paymasterAndData = paymasterAndData;

        paymentMasterNew.validatePaymasterUserOp(userOp, bytes32(uint256(1)), 0); // standart signature

        // standart sig: 0xe34...b2a0a094...6c1c
        // short sig(to2098format): 0xe34...baa0a094...6c

        bytes memory shortSig2098 = hex"e3402d57abf681838763887091f7d4fbb52cd03073a375dd010a1dd0e251f87baa0a0948e6a3579f7b88876286d372aaaf46f2af8e4db9a2a59845130d174a6c";

        paymasterAndData = abi.encodePacked(user1, shortSig2098);

        userOp.paymasterAndData = paymasterAndData;

        paymentMasterNew.validatePaymasterUserOp(userOp, bytes32(uint256(1)), 0); // same signature(eip2098 format)
    }

```

![ecdsa_result.jpg](https://halbornmainframe.com/proxy/audits/images/659eaf1da1aa3698c0ec8c44)

##### Score

Impact: 4  
Likelihood: 4

##### Recommendation

**SOLVED:** The `Biconomy team` solved this finding by upgrading the `@openzeppelin/contracts` package version to `4.7.3`.

`Commit ID:` [b813a60a8475672c2a2d00b7ef5d1839461eaa3e](https://github.com/bcnmy/scw-contracts/commit/b813a60a8475672c2a2d00b7ef5d1839461eaa3e)
summary: The report describes a vulnerability found in the `ECDSA` library developed by the OpenZeppelin team. This vulnerability allows for signature malleability, which means that a user can take a signature that has already been used and submit it again in a different form, bypassing any protection measures. The vulnerability was found in the `recover` and `tryRecover` functions, which accept both standard and compact signature formats. This issue affects contracts that implement signature reuse or replay protection. The report also mentions that the Biconomy contracts were using the vulnerable `ECDSA` library. The report provides a code example to demonstrate the issue and recommends upgrading the `@openzeppelin/contracts` package to version `4.7.3` to solve the problem. The Biconomy team has already addressed the issue by upgrading the package.

title: REENTRANCY LEADS DRAIN OF FUNDS (PRIVILEGED USER)
summary: The report describes a bug in the LiquidityPool contract where a malicious owner or liquidity provider can drain all funds from the pool. This is known as a Reentrancy vulnerability and it can be exploited to steal funds from the contract. The steps to reproduce the bug include deploying the contract, transferring funds to it, and then setting up a malicious attack contract to drain the funds. The bug has been classified as critical and a fix has been implemented by the Biconomy team.

title: WRONG FEE CALCULATION LEADS LOSS OF REWARD FUNDS
summary: The bug report is about a contract called `LiquidityPool` which has two functions to claim gas fees, one for ERC20 tokens and one for the native token. However, there is a problem with the function for claiming gas fees for the native token, which makes it impossible to withdraw the fees. This is because of an error in the calculation of the fee amount in the function. The code for this function can be found in the `LiquidityPool.sol` file. The `Biconomy team` has solved this issue by correcting the math operation that was causing the loss of funds. The impact and likelihood of this bug are both rated as 5. The solution can be found in the `fab4b8c0a10a3e0185b2a06b10248391837c07de` commit ID.

title: INADEQUATE ACCESS CONTROL IN ADDGASFEE FUNCTION ALLOWS TO STEAL USERS' TOKENS
summary: The report describes a security issue where an attacker can use a function in the CCMPSendMessageFacet contract to steal ERC20 tokens from users who have approved the CCMPGateway to manage their tokens. This can happen in any chain where there is a gateway, and even if the tokens were expected to be used in later transactions. The attacker can also front-run the transaction if needed. The report includes a proof of concept showing how the attack can be carried out. The code location of the vulnerable function is also provided, along with a score of 5 for both impact and likelihood of the attack.

title: USDC OF THE INTERNAL BALANCE CAN BE DRAINED BY ANY USER THROUGH THE FERTILIZERFACET.MINTFERTILIZER FUNCTION
summary: The `FertilizerFacet` has a function called `mintFertilizer()` that allows users to buy Fertilizer using USDC. However, there is a bug where the value returned by the `receiveToken()` function is not checked, which means users can exploit this and use the USDC from other users' internal balance to buy Fertilizer. This issue has a high impact and likelihood of occurring. The recommendation is to update the code to check the return value of `receiveToken()` to prevent this exploit. This issue has been solved by the Beanstalk team by updating the code to consider the return value of `receiveToken()`.

title: INTERNAL BALANCE TOKENS CAN BE DRAINED THROUGH THE CURVEFACET.EXCHANGEUNDERLYING FUNCTION
summary: The report describes a bug in the CurveFacet contract, specifically in the `exchangeUnderlying()` function. This function is used to swap underlying assets from different Curve stable pools. The bug allows users to swap tokens that belong to other users, resulting in stolen tokens. The bug occurs when a user sets the `fromMode` to `INTERNAL_TOLERANT` and the value returned by the `receiveToken()` call is not checked. This can be abused by users to swap tokens that belong to other users. The report provides details of the pool and underlying tokens involved in the bug, along with the steps to reproduce it. It also includes a screenshot showing the stolen tokens. The bug has been assigned an impact and likelihood score of 5, and the recommendation is to overwrite `amountIn` with the value returned from the `receiveToken()` call to solve the issue. The Beanstalk team has already implemented this solution.

title: DONATE CALL BEFORE DEPOSIT LEADS LOSS OF POSSIBLE REWARDS
summary: There is a bug in the `donate()` function of the Alluvial contract. If the `totalSupply()` is zero, the function will not mint any rewards. This is because the contract tries to mint rewards for operators according to the `_onEarnings` function, which will always return zero if the contract does not have any LsETH. This means that if someone donates while the `totalSupply()` is zero, no rewards will be given. This issue has been solved by adding another control to the contract.

title: H-7: cannot forward extra rewards from both OCY_Convex to OCT_YDL.
description:
Source: https://github.com/sherlock-audit/2024-03-zivoe-judging/issues/479 

## Found by 
0xpiken, AllTooWell, BoRonGod, Drynooo, Ironsidesec, den\_sosnovskyi, ether\_sky
## Summary

Convex specifies `rewardContract` to be a `VirtualBalanceRewardPool`, but all three OCY_Convex uses it as a ERC20 token, which make it impossible to claim extra rewards and forward them to the OCT_YDL.

## Vulnerability Detail

According to [Convex doc](https://docs.convexfinance.com/convexfinanceintegration/baserewardpool#extra-rewards):

> The BaseRewardPool has an array of child reward contracts called extraRewards.
> You can query the number of extra rewards via baseRewardPool.extraRewardsLength().
> This array holds a list of [VirtualBalanceRewardPool ](https://github.com/convex-eth/platform/blob/main/contracts/contracts/VirtualBalanceRewardPool.sol)contracts which are similar in nature to the base reward contract but without actual control of staked tokens.
> 
> This means that if a pool has CRV rewards as well as SNX rewards, the pool's main reward contract(BaseRewardPool) will distribute the CRV and the child contract(VirtualBalanceRewardPool) will distribute the SNX.

But, in current implementation: (take OCY_Convex_A for example)

        // Extra Rewards
        if (extra) {
            uint256 extraRewardsLength = IBaseRewardPool_OCY_Convex_A(convexRewards).extraRewardsLength();
            for (uint256 i = 0; i < extraRewardsLength; i++) {
                address rewardContract = IBaseRewardPool_OCY_Convex_A(convexRewards).extraRewards(i);
                uint256 rewardAmount = IBaseRewardPool_OCY_Convex_A(rewardContract).rewardToken().balanceOf(
                    address(this)
                );
                //@Audit rewardContract is a VirtualBalanceRewardPool
                if (rewardAmount > 0) { IERC20(rewardContract).safeTransfer(OCT_YDL, rewardAmount); }
            }
        }

Tokens cannot be sent to YDL.

## Impact

Current OCY_Convex_A, OCY_Convex_B and OCY_Convex_C cannot forward extraRewards to YDL.

## Code Snippet

https://github.com/sherlock-audit/2024-03-zivoe/blob/main/zivoe-core-foundry/src/lockers/OCY/OCY_Convex_A.sol#L263
https://docs.convexfinance.com/convexfinanceintegration/baserewardpool#extra-rewards

## Tool used

Manual Review

## Recommendation

Use the real token address for token transfer.






## Discussion

**sherlock-admin4**

1 comment(s) were left on this issue during the judging contest.

**panprog** commented:
> high, dup of #477, loss of additional reward from convex. Since it accumulates over 30-days period, the loss will be significant. Both `balanceOf` and `safeTransfer` are incorrect - they should be called on `rewardToken().token()`. Different dups of this mention either `balanceOf` or `safeTransfer`, but not both, but I consider them to be the same root cause, so all are dups.
summary:
This bug report is about an issue found in the code of a project called OCY_Convex, which is used for managing rewards in a cryptocurrency platform. The issue was found by a group of security experts and reported on GitHub. 

The problem is that the code specifies a certain type of reward contract, but it is being used in a different way, which makes it impossible to claim extra rewards and forward them to another part of the platform. This is a vulnerability that could lead to a loss of rewards for users. 

The team behind the project has provided documentation on how this type of contract should work, but the current implementation is different. This means that the code is not functioning as intended and tokens cannot be transferred to the designated location. 

This issue affects multiple parts of the project and could result in a significant loss of rewards over a period of time. The code snippet provided in the report shows where the problem lies. 

The team used a manual review to find this issue and has recommended using the correct token address for transfers. 

During the judging process, it was noted that this issue has been reported before and is a duplicate of another issue. This could mean that it is a recurring problem that has not been fixed.

title: H-6: Protocol unable to get extra Rewards in OCY_Convex_C
description:
Source: https://github.com/sherlock-audit/2024-03-zivoe-judging/issues/477 

## Found by 
BoRonGod, cergyk
## Summary

Convex would wrap `rewardToken` for pools with IDs 151+, but the counting logic in `OCY_Convex_C.sol` makes it impossible for zivoe to forward yield.

## Vulnerability Detail

In `OCY_Convex_C.sol `, A convex pool with id `270` is used: 

    /// @dev Convex information.
    address public convexDeposit = 0xF403C135812408BFbE8713b5A23a04b3D48AAE31;
    address public convexPoolToken = 0x383E6b4437b59fff47B619CBA855CA29342A8559;
    address public convexRewards = 0xc583e81bB36A1F620A804D8AF642B63b0ceEb5c0;

    uint256 public convexPoolID = 270;

In the following logic, `rewardContract` is defaulted to the address of extraRewards. This assumption is fine for pools with PoolId < 150, but would not work for IDs 151+.

    /// @notice Claims rewards and forward them to the OCT_YDL.
    /// @param extra Flag for claiming extra rewards.
    function claimRewards(bool extra) public nonReentrant {
        IBaseRewardPool_OCY_Convex_C(convexRewards).getReward();

        // Native Rewards (CRV, CVX)
        uint256 rewardsCRV = IERC20(CRV).balanceOf(address(this));
        uint256 rewardsCVX = IERC20(CVX).balanceOf(address(this));
        if (rewardsCRV > 0) { IERC20(CRV).safeTransfer(OCT_YDL, rewardsCRV); }
        if (rewardsCVX > 0) { IERC20(CVX).safeTransfer(OCT_YDL, rewardsCVX); }

        // Extra Rewards
        if (extra) {
            uint256 extraRewardsLength = IBaseRewardPool_OCY_Convex_C(convexRewards).extraRewardsLength();
            for (uint256 i = 0; i < extraRewardsLength; i++) {
                address rewardContract = IBaseRewardPool_OCY_Convex_C(convexRewards).extraRewards(i); 
                //@Audit incorrect here!
                uint256 rewardAmount = IBaseRewardPool_OCY_Convex_C(rewardContract).rewardToken().balanceOf(address(this));
                if (rewardAmount > 0) { IERC20(rewardContract).safeTransfer(OCT_YDL, rewardAmount); }
            }
        }
    }


According to [convex doc](https://docs.convexfinance.com/convexfinanceintegration/baserewardpool#:~:text=Important%20for%20pools,wrappers/ConvexStakingWrapper.sol), 

> for pools with IDs 151+:
> VirtualBalanceRewardPool's rewardToken points to a wrapped version of the underlying token.  This Token implementation can be found here: https://github.com/convex-eth/platform/blob/main/contracts/contracts/StashTokenWrapper.sol

Just check `convexRewards` of pool 270: 

https://etherscan.io/address/0xc583e81bB36A1F620A804D8AF642B63b0ceEb5c0#readContract#F5

For index 0, it returns a [`VirtualBalanceRewardPool`](https://etherscan.io/address/0x22A0a706Aa423E2257e4217be2268e0374b9229f) with [rewardtoken](https://etherscan.io/address/0xc583e81bB36A1F620A804D8AF642B63b0ceEb5c0#readContract#F19) = 0x85D81Ee851D36423A5784CD3Cb6f1a1193Cb5978. This contract is a `StashTokenWrapper`, which is consistent with what the convex documentation says.

And, when `IBaseRewardPool_OCY_Convex_C(convexRewards).getReward();` is triggered, reward tokens will be unwrapped and send to caller, so rewardAmount will always return 0, means such yield cannot be claimed for zivoe.

                address rewardContract = IBaseRewardPool_OCY_Convex_C(convexRewards).extraRewards(i); 

                //@Audit incorrect here! `rewardToken` is a `StashTokenWrapper`, not the reward token!

                uint256 rewardAmount = IBaseRewardPool_OCY_Convex_C(rewardContract).rewardToken().balanceOf(address(this));
                if (rewardAmount > 0) { IERC20(rewardContract).safeTransfer(OCT_YDL, rewardAmount); }

## Impact

Users will lose extra rewards from convex pools with IDs 151+.

## Code Snippet

https://github.com/sherlock-audit/2024-03-zivoe/blob/main/zivoe-core-foundry/src/lockers/OCY/OCY_Convex_C.sol#L210-L219
https://docs.convexfinance.com/convexfinanceintegration/baserewardpool

## Tool used

Manual Review

title: H-4: Revoking vesting schedule does not subtract user votes correctly
description:
Source: https://github.com/sherlock-audit/2024-03-zivoe-judging/issues/118 

## Found by 
0xAnmol, 0xpiken, 0xvj, 9oelm, Afriaudit, Ironsidesec, JigglypuffAndPikachu, KingNFT, KupiaSec, Ruhum, SilverChariot, Tendency, Tychai0s, Varun\_05, amar, denzi\_, dimulski, ether\_sky, lemonmon, marchev, mt030d, rbserver, saidam017, sakshamguruji, samuraii77
## Summary
[ZivoeVestingRewards.revokeVestingSchedule()](https://github.com/sherlock-audit/2024-03-zivoe/blob/d4111645b19a1ad3ccc899bea073b6f19be04ccd/zivoe-core-foundry/src/ZivoeRewardsVesting.sol#L429-L467) should reduce the voting power of the user with the withdrawable amount plus the revoked amount. However, it reduces it only by the withdrawable amount.

## Vulnerability Detail
When called, `revokeVestingSchedule()` fetches the withdrawable amount by the user at that moment.
```solidity
        uint256 amount = amountWithdrawable(account);
```

The revoke logic is executed and the user's checkpoint value is decreased by `amount`.
```solidity
        _writeCheckpoint(_checkpoints[account], _subtract, amount);
```

The code ignores the amount that's being revoked and the user keeps more voting power than he has to.
Imagine the following:
`totalVested = 1000`
`withdrawable = 0`

If the schedule gets revoked, the user's checkpoint value will not be decreased at all because there is nothing to be withdrawn. The user can later use their voting power to vote on governance proposals.

In fact, `amountWithdrawable(account)` being close to 0 has a very high likelihood because:
   - the user can frontrun the transaction and withdraw the tokens they are entitled to
   -  it's highly likely that a vesting schedule will be removed shortly after creating it.

However, even if `amountWithdrawable()` is not equal to 0, the user would still be left with more voting power.
## Impact
Users keep voting power that must have been taken away.

## Code Snippet
POC to be run in [Test_ZivoeRewardsVesting.sol](https://github.com/sherlock-audit/2024-03-zivoe/blob/main/zivoe-core-testing/src/TESTS_Core/Test_ZivoeRewardsVesting.sol)
```solidity
    function test_revoking_leaves_votes() public {
       assert(zvl.try_createVestingSchedule(
            address(vestZVE), 
            address(moe), 
            0, 
            360,
            6000 ether, 
            true
        ));
        // Vesting succeeded
        assertEq(vestZVE.balanceOf(address(moe)), 6000 ether);

        hevm.roll(block.number + 1);
     
        // User votes have increased
        assertEq(vestZVE.getPastVotes(address(moe), block.number - 1), 6000 ether);

        assert(zvl.try_revokeVestingSchedule(address(vestZVE), address(moe)));
        // Revoking succeeded
        assertEq(vestZVE.balanceOf(address(moe)), 0);

        hevm.roll(block.number + 1);
        // User votes have not been decreased at all
        assertEq(vestZVE.getPastVotes(address(moe), block.number - 1), 6000 ether);
    }
```

## Tool used

Foundry

## Recommendation
Subtract the correct amount from the checkpoint's value
```diff
-        _writeCheckpoint(_checkpoints[account], _subtract, amount);
+       _writeCheckpoint(_checkpoints[account], _subtract, vestingAmount - vestingScheduleOf[account].totalWithdrawn + amount)
```




## Discussion

**sherlock-admin4**

1 comment(s) were left on this issue during the judging contest.

**panprog** commented:
> high, incorrect checkpoints amount subtracted during `revokeVestingSchedule` causes permanent inflated amount of user votes.



**pseudonaut**

Recommended suggestion seems incorrect

It doesn't address the totalSupplyCheckpoints right above that line (both should be in tandem):

```solidity
_writeCheckpoint(_totalSupplyCheckpoints, _subtract, vestingAmount - vestingScheduleOf[account].totalWithdrawn + amount);
_writeCheckpoint(_checkpoints[account], _subtract, vestingAmount - vestingScheduleOf[account].totalWithdrawn + amount);
```


**sherlock-admin2**

The protocol team fixed this issue in the following PRs/commits:
https://github.com/Zivoe/zivoe-core-foundry/pull/268

The report includes a code snippet and a recommendation to fix the issue by subtracting the correct amount from the checkpoint's value. The tool used to find this bug was Foundry. title: Denial Of Slashing
summary: This report discusses a vulnerability in the verifyDoubleSigning function, which can be exploited by a malicious operator to evade slashing. This vulnerability is due to the linear complexity of the function, which can be increased indefinitely by repeatedly calling the updateDelegation function. title: Full Deleverage Functionality Can Be Permanently Bricked
description:
In the [`seaportCallback4878572495` function](https://github.com/Ion-Protocol/ion-seaport/blob/54110bbfbe56d18390d4e9c9f8fc9fb973500da6/src/SeaportDeleverage.sol#L266) within the [`SeaportDeleverage`](https://github.com/Ion-Protocol/ion-seaport/blob/54110bbfbe56d18390d4e9c9f8fc9fb973500da6/src/SeaportDeleverage.sol#L82) contract, there is [a requirement](https://github.com/Ion-Protocol/ion-seaport/blob/54110bbfbe56d18390d4e9c9f8fc9fb973500da6/src/SeaportDeleverage.sol#L290) that the `BASE` token balance of the contract is `0` after a full deleverage.


However, this will always revert if a user has independently transferred any amount of `BASE` tokens into the [`SeaportDeleverage`](https://github.com/Ion-Protocol/ion-seaport/blob/54110bbfbe56d18390d4e9c9f8fc9fb973500da6/src/SeaportDeleverage.sol#L82) contract. Since there is no way to transfer the tokens out of the contract, a single transfer will permanently brick the contract.


Consider removing this check, or modifying it to instead check that the token balance of the contract has not changed since the beginning of the execution flow. Alternatively, consider either modifying the logic to transfer all unneeded `BASE` tokens to the user, or implementing a "rescue" function to remove stranded `BASE` tokens.


***Update:** Resolved in [pull request #3](https://github.com/Ion-Protocol/ion-seaport/pull/3). The sanity check was removed to prevent bricking of the contract.*
summary: The report states that there is a bug in the code for the `SeaportDeleverage` contract, specifically in the `seaportCallback4878572495` function. This function has a requirement that the `BASE` token balance of the contract must be `0` after a full deleverage. However, if a user has transferred any amount of `BASE` tokens into the contract, this requirement will always fail and the contract will be permanently unusable. The report suggests removing this requirement or modifying it to check for changes in the token balance instead. Another solution proposed is to transfer any unneeded `BASE` tokens back to the user or implementing a "rescue" function to remove stranded tokens. The bug has been resolved in a recent update.

title: Attacker Can Stall Undelegations
description:
The process of undelegating assets from a subject in the [`FortaStakingVault` contract](https://github.com/NethermindEth/forta-staking-vault/blob/ce87cffbf813e27cc83157933760b51fa44a1885/src/FortaStakingVault.sol) requires two steps:


Firstly, the `operator` triggers the undelegation process by calling the [`initiateUndelegate` function](https://github.com/NethermindEth/forta-staking-vault/blob/ce87cffbf813e27cc83157933760b51fa44a1885/src/FortaStakingVault.sol#L201), which [deploys a distributor instance](https://github.com/NethermindEth/forta-staking-vault/blob/ce87cffbf813e27cc83157933760b51fa44a1885/src/FortaStakingVault.sol#L209), an ERC-20 token. The vault transfers its `FortaStaking` shares in the given subject to the distributor, and in return, receives minted distributor tokens that represent its position and are equivalent to the `FortaStaking` shares transferred to the distributor contract. The distributor also [initiates the withdrawal](https://github.com/NethermindEth/forta-staking-vault/blob/ce87cffbf813e27cc83157933760b51fa44a1885/src/InactiveSharesDistributor.sol#L65) of the assets in the `FortaStaking` contract and the waiting period is stored in the Vault for that particular subject.


Secondly, once the waiting period passes, users are permitted to call the [`undelegate` function](https://github.com/NethermindEth/forta-staking-vault/blob/ce87cffbf813e27cc83157933760b51fa44a1885/src/FortaStakingVault.sol#L233) to undelegate all the staked tokens of a specific subject by the vault. However, a problem arises when calculating the amount of FORT tokens to be sent from the distributor back to the vault. Instead of using the amount returned by the [`withdraw` function](https://github.com/NethermindEth/forta-staking-vault/blob/ce87cffbf813e27cc83157933760b51fa44a1885/src/InactiveSharesDistributor.sol#L74) from the `FortaStaking` contract, the balance of [FORT tokens held by the distributor will be used instead](https://github.com/NethermindEth/forta-staking-vault/blob/ce87cffbf813e27cc83157933760b51fa44a1885/src/InactiveSharesDistributor.sol#L75) which can be manipulated since anyone can send FORT tokens to the distributor.


If this occurs, the `undelegate` function will revert when [attempting to subtract the assets](https://github.com/NethermindEth/forta-staking-vault/blob/ce87cffbf813e27cc83157933760b51fa44a1885/src/FortaStakingVault.sol#L259) delegated to the given subject since the amount subtracted will be greater than the one tracked in the `_assetsPerSubject` variable. This implies that the funds deposited in the distributor will become inaccessible and any subsequent attempts to invoke the `undelegate` function for that particular subject will fail.


Nonetheless, this is not irreversible as the operator can allocate additional tokens to the subject, thereby increasing the `_assetsPerSubject` amount to prevent an underflow. However, it may take some time before the operator notices this problem and the attacker could front-run any future delegations to put the undelegation process in a stalled situation again. A step-by-step proof-of-concept for this scenario can be found in [this secret gist](https://gist.github.com/jbcarpanelli/6712c1c882e30263d6e34e08b4808f9b).


Consider using the amount returned by the [`withdraw` function](https://github.com/NethermindEth/forta-staking-vault/blob/ce87cffbf813e27cc83157933760b51fa44a1885/src/InactiveSharesDistributor.sol#L74) from the `FortaStaking` contract instead of the balance of FORT held by the distributor.


***Update:** Resolved in [pull request #24](https://github.com/NethermindEth/forta-staking-vault/pull/24).*
summary: This bug report discusses an issue with the undelegation process in the FortaStakingVault contract. This process involves two steps: the operator initiates the undelegation process by transferring shares to a distributor contract and then, once the waiting period has passed, users can call the undelegate function to receive their staked tokens back. However, there is a problem with the calculation of the amount of FORT tokens to be sent back to the vault. Instead of using the amount returned by the withdraw function from the FortaStaking contract, the balance of FORT tokens held by the distributor is used, which can be manipulated by anyone. This can cause the undelegate function to fail and make the funds deposited in the distributor inaccessible. This can be fixed by using the amount returned by the withdraw function instead of the balance of FORT held by the distributor. This issue has been resolved in a recent pull request.

title: Incomplete Implementation of ERC-4626 Base Contract Leading to Asset Management and Usability Issues
description:
The vault contract's adaptation from the ERC-4626 standard demonstrates critical flaws in asset management and functionality due to incomplete overrides of essential functions. Initially, the primary concern centers around the `mint` function. When users invoke the function, the contract correctly emits shares. However, it fails to update the [\_totalAssets](https://github.com/NethermindEth/forta-staking-vault/blob/ce87cffbf813e27cc83157933760b51fa44a1885/src/FortaStakingVault.sol#L47) variable and the pool's asset holdings. This discrepancy leads to a significant issue: the vault's asset tracking becomes inaccurate, which in turn will result in incorrect calculations when users attempt to redeem their shares.


Similarly, the omission of an override for the `withdraw` function can lead to transactions reverting when users attempt to execute withdrawals. Although this issue has a minor direct impact compared to the asset management flaw, it contributes to a degraded user experience, potentially deterring user interaction with the contract.


Consider modifying the `mint` and `withdraw` functions from the `ERC-4626Upgradeable` contract within the `FortaStakingVault` contract to accurately reflect withdrawn and minted assets in the `_totalAssets` variable.


***Update:** Resolved in [pull request #22](https://github.com/NethermindEth/forta-staking-vault/pull/22).*
summary: The vault contract, which manages assets, has critical flaws that affect its functionality. The main issue is with the `mint` function, which correctly gives users shares but does not update the total assets and pool holdings. This leads to inaccurate tracking of assets and incorrect calculations for users trying to redeem shares. Another problem is the lack of an override for the `withdraw` function, which can cause transactions to fail and make it difficult for users to interact with the contract. To fix these issues, the `mint` and `withdraw` functions need to be modified to accurately reflect the total assets in the contract. This problem has been resolved in a recent update.

title: getOraclePrice is prone to manipulation
description:
## Vulnerability Assessment

## Context
**File:** VeloOracle.sol  
**Line:** 70

## Description
The `getOraclePrice` function is used to retrieve the latest price from a Velodrome pool. There is a faulty assumption that if the latest observation's timestamp is in the past, the `slot0` price can't have been manipulated, and thus it is returned with no extra checks made. The problem arises because Velodrome pools write observations once every 15 seconds, allowing for a manipulated price with an outdated observation.

```solidity
if (block.timestamp != blockTimestamp)
    return (spotSqrtPriceX96, spotTick);
```

## Recommendation
Use the latest observation price only if more than 15 seconds have passed since the last observation.

## Additional Notes
- **Mellow:** Fixed in commit `736eef90`.
- **Cantina Managed:** Fixed in commit `736eef90`. Oracle now always returns the spot price. It is important for external protocols to not simply rely on the price returned here, but rather also make a call to `ensureNoMEV`.
summary: The bug report is about a faulty assumption in the code of VeloOracle.sol, specifically in line 70. The function getOraclePrice is used to get the latest price from a Velodrome pool. However, the code assumes that if the latest observation's timestamp is in the past, the price cannot be manipulated and is returned without any additional checks. This is a problem because Velodrome pools only update their observations every 15 seconds, which leaves room for a manipulated price to be returned. The recommendation is to only use the latest observation price if more than 15 seconds have passed since the last update. This bug has been fixed in commit 736eef90 by both Mellow and Cantina Managed. The risk level of this bug is considered medium. It is important for external protocols to not solely rely on the price returned by this function, but also make a call to ensure that there is no manipulation.
